definition_zh: 眼睛；眼状物；视力；眼光；注意
definition_en: the organ of sight, or the power, judgment, shape, or watchfulness associated with it
core_image: 一只圆润的眼球映出世界的倒影，目光像一道细线把人与被看之物连起来
scene: 学生在实验室先戴上护目镜，然后才开始观察火焰颜色的变化。Put on the goggles first, then observe the flame colour with your own eye.
sceneCN: 这里指「视觉器官」，对应第 1 个义项：眼睛本身；句意为先戴护目镜再用眼睛观察火焰颜色。画面要点：护目镜的弧面、实验室桌台、跳动的火焰。

pos.zh: 眼睛；视力；眼光；眼状物；注意

derivatives.zh: 眼球（基础词与「球」一词的复合名词，指眼睛的球状本体）
眉毛（基础词与「眉毛位置」一词的复合名词，指眼睛上方的毛）
睫毛（基础词与「鞭梢状毛」一词的复合名词，指眼睑边缘的细毛）
目击者（基础词与「证人」一词的复合名词，指亲眼所见的人）
视力（基础词与「视觉」一词的复合名词，指眼睛的功能）

senses.title: The organ of sight
senses.definition: the round organ of the body that receives light and makes seeing possible
senses.definitionCN: 身体接收光线、使视觉成为可能的圆形器官
senses.example: She shaded her eyes from the sun.
senses.why: The body part is the concrete anchor; every other meaning is a picture built on the act of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位是具体锚点；其余所有义项都是从「看」这一动作上搭建的画面。

senses.title: The power or act of seeing
senses.definition: the ability to see, or an act of looking
senses.definitionCN: 视力，或看的行为
senses.example: The old hawk still has a keen eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这只老鹰视力依然敏锐。
senses.why: Once the organ stands for seeing, the word can name the faculty itself without mentioning the body.
senses.whyCN: 器官既已代表「看」，这个词就能不提身体而直接指称能力本身。

senses.title: A way of judging or noticing
senses.definition: a personal skill at noticing or judging a particular quality
senses.definitionCN: 对某种特质进行识别或评判的个人能力
senses.example: She has an eye for colour.
senses.why: Seeing well implies judging well; the faculty of sight is borrowed as a metaphor for taste.
senses.whyCN: 看得准意味着判断得准；视觉能力被借来隐喻鉴赏力。

senses.title: Something shaped like an eye
senses.definition: a hole, loop, or mark that resembles the shape of an eye
senses.definitionCN: 形状类似眼睛的孔、环或斑点
senses.example: The needle has a small eye at its tip.
senses.exampleCN: 针尖上有一个小小的针眼。
senses.why: The round outline of the organ gives its name to any similar round opening or spot.
senses.whyCN: 器官的圆形轮廓被用来命名一切类似的圆孔或圆点。

senses.title: Watchful attention
senses.definition: careful attention given by watching something closely
senses.definitionCN: 通过密切注视给予的仔细关注
senses.example: Keep an eye on the soup.
senses.why: The organ that watches becomes the watch itself: the idiom treats attention as an organ set on its target.
senses.whyCN: 负责看东西的器官演变成「注视」本身：习语把注意力当作一只安放在目标上的眼睛。

intro.en: Eye is one of the shortest core body words in English, with a lineage that runs straight back through Old English to a reconstructed Germanic root.
intro.cn: eye 是英语中最短的核心身体词之一，谱系经古英语一直回溯到重构的日耳曼语根。

items.en: The reconstructed root augon or ahan is taken to mean 'to see'; German Auge shows the same stock.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 augon 或 ahan 意为「看见」；德语 Auge 出自同一语族。

items.en: Norse auga reinforced the same vowel pattern in the northern dialects of England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 auga 在英格兰北方方言里加固了同样的元音形态。

items.en: Old English eage, ege carried the sense already; the word has been monosyllabic in most contexts for a very long time.
items.cn: 古英语 eage、ege 已承载此义；这个词在多数语境里很早就是单音节。

items.en: Middle English ye and eye competed in spelling before the modern form settled.
items.cn: 中古英语 ye 与 eye 在拼写上竞争过，之后现代形式才稳定。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling eye, and the word grew rich idioms: keep an eye on, see eye to eye.
items.cn: 现代英语固定拼写 eye，并长出丰富习语：keep an eye on（留意）、see eye to eye（看法一致）。

note.en: Look-alikes share the letter shape or the root; near-meaning words occupy the same field of seeing and attention.
note.cn: 形近组共享字母外形或词根；近义组占据「看与注意」的同一个义场。

entries.definition: an old way of saying yes in voting or sailing
entries.definitionCN: 投票或航海中说「赞成」的旧说法；只是同音，与眼睛无关

entries.definition: to colour cloth or hair with a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 给布料或头发上色；拼写仅一字母之差，词源不同

entries.definition: the Greek root for circle that also appears in words for the eye socket
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语表「圆」的词根，也见于眼窝等词；与 eye 属不同语系

entries.definition: the ability or sense of sight
entries.definitionCN: 视力；视觉能力
长时间的凝视
注视某物

normalIntro.en: Five everyday handles for the shortest seeing word.
normalIntro.cn: 关于这个最短的「看」词的五个日常抓手。

normal.en: The word has only three letters, and the shape itself looks like a tiny face with two pupils.
normal.cn: 单词只有三个字母，字形本身像一颗头与两只瞳孔的简笔画。

normal.en: keep an eye on is one of the highest-frequency watch phrases in everyday English.
normal.cn: keep an eye on 是英语最高频的照看短语，留意一下身边标语就能碰到。

normal.en: see eye to eye means agreeing, because two aligned gazes picture two aligned minds.
normal.cn: see eye to eye 意为「意见一致」，两人目光对齐即想法对齐。

normal.en: German Auge is a cousin, so the short word has a long Germanic pedigree.
normal.cn: 德语 Auge 与它同源，都是「看」的古老短词。

normal.en: apple of my eye names a cherished person, from the old belief that the pupil holds the dearest image.
normal.cn: apple of my eye 意为「心肝宝贝」，古代把瞳孔里映出的人视为最珍视之物。

abstract.en: Picture the world as a painting and the eye as the only plug that carries it into the mind.
abstract.cn: 想象世界是一幅画，眼睛是唯一把画接进心里的插头。

abstract.en: Attention is an eye sent out: whatever it lands on lights up.
abstract.cn: 注意力像一只被派出去的眼睛，落在哪件事上，哪件事就被照亮。

abstract.en: Your vision is a trained filter: you see what you have taught yourself to notice.
abstract.cn: 眼光是记忆里的滤镜：你看见什么，取决于你训练过自己注意什么。

examples.en: Keep an eye on the kettle while I answer the phone.
examples.cn: 我去接电话时帮我留意水壶。

examples.en: She has an eye for detail, so her reports are always accurate.
examples.cn: 她对细节有眼光，所以报告总是很准确。

examples.en: The camera is the eye of the documentary, always watching quietly.
examples.cn: 镜头是纪录片的眼睛，一直安静地注视。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱」——眼睛爱看美好的东西，所以一想到 eye 就想到「爱看」。

root: 来自原始日耳曼语表「看」的词根（重构形式 augon/ahan，一般认为），经古英语 eage 演化而来；德语 Auge、古诺斯语 auga 同族。词义从「看」扩展出眼光、眼状物与注意等比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: From the organ itself outward to faculty, judgment, shape, and attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 从器官本体向外扩展到能力、判断、形状与注意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round organ that connects the mind to the world through light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗借光线把心灵与世界连起来的圆形器官。

branches.en: THE ORGAN: the body part that receives light.
branches.cn: 器官：接收光线的身体部位。

branches.en: THE FACULTY: seeing as an ability.
branches.cn: 能力：看这一本领。

branches.en: THE JUDGMENT: taste and discernment borrowed from sight.
branches.cn: 判断：借自视觉的鉴赏力。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: round openings named after the organ.
branches.cn: 形状：以器官命名的圆形孔环。

branches.en: THE WATCHING: attention expressed as a set eye.
branches.cn: 注视：以眼睛表达的注意。

intro.en: Eye travels inside compounds faster than it takes affixes; the family is built by pairing.
intro.cn: eye 更多进入复合词而非加缀；词族靠并置构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin used a different word for the eye, so there are no Latin siblings here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用别的词表示眼睛，因此没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: the eyeball moves in its socket

items.meaning: a short hair at the edge
items.example: one eyelash fell on her cheek

items.meaning: the hollow that holds the eye
items.example: the glass eye fits the socket
the needle's eye-hole takes the thread

definition_zh: 脸；面孔；表面；面对；朝向；体面
definition_en: the front of the head, the visible surface of a thing, or the act of turning toward and dealing with something
core_image: 一张朝向世界的正脸：别人从这张脸读到情绪，而墙和钟也有自己的「正脸」
scene: 下课后老师提醒大家，下周要当众发言，紧张也要提前练习。Next week you must face the audience and speak with confidence.
sceneCN: 这里指「面对、正视」，对应第 4 个义项：迎向困难局面并应对；句意为下周要面对听众自信发言。画面要点：讲台、台下目光、深呼吸的手势。

derivatives.zh: 面部的（基础词加形容词后缀，指与脸有关）
表面（前缀 sur-「在上方」加词根 fac「面」，指物体外层）
饰面；朝向（动词的名词化，指覆盖正面的材料或方向）
整修；翻新（基础词与「提升」一词的复合名词，原指面部整容，引申为外观翻新）
虚伪的（复合形容词，指有两张脸，即表里不一）

senses.title: The front of the head
senses.definition: the front part of the head from the forehead to the chin
senses.definitionCN: 头部从额头到下巴的前面部分
senses.example: Her face turned red with cold.
senses.why: The body part is the historical core; Latin already used facies for this.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位是历史核心；拉丁语 facies 已作此解。

senses.title: The surface that is shown
senses.definition: the front or visible surface of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 事物的正面或可见表面
senses.example: The face of the clock is cracked.
senses.why: A thing's front is its 'head-side'; the human face models this for every object.
senses.whyCN: 物的正面就是它的「头面」；人脸为一切物提供了模型。

senses.title: To stand or turn toward
senses.definition: to be positioned with the front toward something
senses.definitionCN: 正面朝向某物地放置
senses.example: Our house faces the sea.
senses.why: The front of a person naturally turns toward what it meets; direction grows from posture.
senses.whyCN: 人的正面自然朝向所遇之物；方向感由姿态长出。

senses.title: To deal with something difficult
senses.definition: to confront and deal with a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 正视并处理困难局面
senses.example: She faced the exam calmly.
senses.why: Meeting difficulty is standing front-to-front with it; confrontation becomes coping.
senses.whyCN: 迎难而上即与困难正面对立；对抗转为应对。

senses.title: Dignity in others' eyes
senses.definition: respect or dignity in social situations
senses.definitionCN: 社交场合中的尊重与尊严
senses.example: He left to save face.
senses.why: The face is what others see; losing what is seen is losing standing.
senses.whyCN: 脸是他人所见；失去所见之物即失去地位。

intro.en: Face came into English through French from Latin facies, the appearance or form a thing presents.
intro.cn: face 经法语由拉丁语 facies（事物呈现的外形）进入英语。

items.en: Latin facies meant shape, appearance, and later the front of the head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 facies 意为外形、样貌，后来指头部正面。

items.en: Old French face kept the head sense and softened to the visible surface.
items.cn: 古法语 face 保留头部之义，并柔化为可见表面。

items.en: Middle English borrowed face in the thirteenth century, both for the head and for fronts of things.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪借入 face，既指头部也指物的正面。

items.en: Modern English turned the noun into a verb: to face a problem, a wall, a rival.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词转为动词：面对问题、朝向墙面、迎战对手。

items.en: French face still carries the head sense in modern French.
items.cn: 现代法语 face 仍保留头部之义。

note.en: Look-alikes share spelling or the Latin root fac; near-meaning words live in the field of confronting and surfaces.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写或拉丁词根 fac；近义组处于「面对与表面」的义场。

entries.definitionCN: 事实；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: one small face of a gem, or one side of a topic
entries.definitionCN: 宝石的小切面，或话题的一个侧面；与 face 同出拉丁词根 fac

entries.definition: the front wall of a building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物的正面；同出拉丁 facies，侧重外观

entries.definition: to face something or someone directly
entries.definitionCN: 正面迎对
遭遇；碰上
正面；前面部分

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a word that names both your head-front and your way of meeting trouble.
normalIntro.cn: 既指脸部正面、又指应对姿态的词，五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin facies means the look a thing presents, so every sense of face grows from a presented front.
normal.cn: 拉丁 facies＝外形；face 的一切义都从「呈现出来的那一面」长出。

normal.en: surface is sur (on top) plus face, literally the top layer that is shown.
normal.cn: surface＝sur（上）+face，字面即「顶上那一面」。

normal.en: lose face and save face came into English from the Chinese idea of losing mianzi.
normal.cn: lose face 保 face 这对短语直接来自汉语「丢脸」的文化概念。

normal.en: face the music means to accept the consequences, like a soldier standing before the drums.
normal.cn: face the music 意为「承担后果」，像兵士临阵听鼓。

normal.en: Clock faces, cliff faces, and façades show that any front can be a face.
normal.cn: 钟面、表脸、山崖面：一切正面都能叫 face。

abstract.en: Emotions are written on the face, so another person's face is the first news you read.
abstract.cn: 情绪写在脸上，所以别人的脸就是你读到的第一条新闻。

abstract.en: Facing trouble is turning your front, not your back, toward the problem.
abstract.cn: 面对困难像转身：把正面而不是背影留给麻烦。

abstract.en: Mianzi is social currency, and spending the last coin is the ugliest moment.
abstract.cn: 面子是社交货币，花光它的那一刻最难看。

examples.en: The two leaders finally met face to face in Geneva.
examples.cn: 两位领导人终于在日内瓦面对面会晤。

examples.en: You must face the fact that the plan needs more money.
examples.cn: 你必须面对这个计划需要更多资金的事实。

examples.en: The window faces south, so the room is bright all day.
examples.cn: 窗户朝南，所以房间整天明亮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费事」——面对问题觉得费事，face 就是「面对」。

root: 拉丁语 facies（外形、脸）经古法语 face 进入中古英语；同根词 surface、facet、facade。名词本义为头的前部，后由「正面」引申出朝向、面对与体面等义。

sensesIntro.en: From the visible front of the head to surfaces, directions, confrontations, and social dignity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头部的可见正面，扩展到表面、方向、对抗与社交尊严。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front that a head or thing turns toward the world.
core.cn: 核心意象：头部或事物朝向世界的那一正面。

branches.en: THE HEAD FRONT: the face as a body part.
branches.cn: 头部正面：作为身体部位的脸。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: any front that can be seen.
branches.cn: 表面：一切可见的正面。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: turning a front toward something.
branches.cn: 方向：把正面转向某物。

branches.en: THE CONFRONTATION: meeting difficulty head-on.
branches.cn: 对抗：正面迎向困难。

branches.en: THE DIGNITY: the self as others see it.
branches.cn: 尊严：他人眼中的自我。

intro.en: Face carries the Latin root fac- (appearance, front) into a family of front-related words.
intro.cn: face 携拉丁词根 fac-（外形、正面）构成一族与「面」相关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facies left direct cousins in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facies 在英语中留下直接同族词。

items.example: the Latin facies is the direct ancestor
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 facies 是直系祖先

items.meaning: the outside layer of a thing
the front wall, the outward show
items.example: the facade hides the old structure

items.meaning: one side of a gem or a question
items.example: every facet of the case was examined
items.exampleCN: 案件每个侧面都被查过

items.example: a facial expression says a lot

items.meaning: without identity or a known face
words said before the main text

definition_zh: 事实；实际；真相；实情
definition_en: a thing known to be true, or something that has actually happened
core_image: 钉在墙上的证据板：每张卡片都是一件已发生过的事，风吹不走
scene: 辩论课前，老师要求每人先核对自己的资料来源，再上台发言。Before the debate, check that every statement in your notes is a fact.
sceneCN: 这里指「已知为真之事」，对应第 1 个义项：可被证明为真的信息；句意为辩论前确认笔记中每条陈述都是事实。画面要点：资料卡、勾选的笔迹、辩论台。

derivatives.zh: 事实的（基础词加形容词后缀，指以事实为准）
事实上（形容词加副词后缀）
实情调查的（复合形容词，指查明事实的）
工厂（词根 fac「做」加名词后缀，指「做东西的地方」）
因素；因子（词根 fac「做」加者缀，指起作用的东西）

senses.title: Something known to be true
senses.definition: a piece of information that can be shown to be true
senses.definitionCN: 能够被证明为真实的信息
senses.example: The report is based on facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告以事实为依据。
senses.why: A deed done leaves evidence; what has truly happened becomes what is known.
senses.whyCN: 做过的事留下证据；真实发生者即已知之事。

senses.title: Truth as opposed to invention
senses.definition: reality rather than imagination or opinion
senses.definitionCN: 实在，而非想象或意见
senses.example: Separate fact from fiction.
senses.why: Done deeds are the hard ground under words; fiction floats above it.
senses.whyCN: 已做之事是言语下的硬地；虚构悬于其上。

senses.title: An event or deed
senses.definition: something that has actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 实际发生过的事情
senses.example: The facts of the case are clear.
senses.why: The oldest Latin sense of factum was the act itself, not the knowledge of it.
senses.whyCN: factum 在拉丁语中最古老的含义就是行为本身，而非对它的认知。

senses.title: A detail used in argument
senses.definition: one item of information used to support a claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑论点的一条信息
senses.example: Give me one fact to prove it.
senses.why: Argument is built from confirmed happenings, one stone at a time.
senses.whyCN: 论证由确证之事一块块垒成。

intro.en: Fact descends from Latin factum, 'a thing done', the past participle of facere, 'to do'.
intro.cn: fact 源自拉丁语 factum（已做成的事），即 facere（做）的过去分词。

items.en: Latin facere meant to do or make; its participle factum named a deed, a thing done.
items.cn: 拉丁语 facere 意为做、造；其分词 factum 指已做之事、行为。

items.en: Medieval Latin used factum for an event or deed recorded in documents.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 factum 指文献中记录的事件或行为。

items.en: Old French fact and fait passed the word on with the sense of an act and its record.
items.cn: 古法语 fact、fait 把「行为及其记录」之义传了下去。

items.en: Middle English took fact in the sixteenth century mainly for a thing known to have happened.
items.cn: 中古英语在十六世纪借入 fact，主要指确已发生之事。

items.en: Modern English widened fact to any verifiable statement, giving in fact, in point of fact.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fact 扩展为一切可核验的陈述，并出现 in fact、in point of fact。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root fac- or spelling; near-meaning words name kinds of truth and reality.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fac- 或拼写；近义组命名各种「真实与事实」。

entries.definition: the Latin root to do or make, seen in factory and factor
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁词根「做」，见于 factory、factor

entries.definition: a single piece of given information
entries.definitionCN: 一条给定的信息

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a word that means a thing already done.
normalIntro.cn: 意为「已做成之事」的词，五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin facere means to do, and factum the thing done, so a fact is what has been done.
normal.cn: 拉丁 facere＝做；factum＝做成了的，所以 fact 就是既成之事。

normal.en: in fact is the highest-frequency emphasis phrase in spoken English.
normal.cn: in fact 是口语最高频的强调短语。

normal.en: factory shares the root: a place where things are done or made.
normal.cn: factory 与 fact 同根：都来自「做」。

normal.en: as a matter of fact sounds a step more formal than in fact.
normal.cn: as a matter of fact 语气比 in fact 更正式。

normal.en: fact and fault differ by one letter: doing right makes a fact, doing wrong a fault.
normal.cn: fact 与 fault 只差字母：做对是事实，做错是过失。

abstract.en: Facts are floor tiles: opinions stand firm only when laid on them.
abstract.cn: 事实像地砖，观点只能铺在地砖上才稳。

abstract.en: Every finished deed is a full stop that cannot be rewritten.
abstract.cn: 每件已完成的事都是一个不再改变的句号。

abstract.en: Truth is a jigsaw puzzle and facts are the pieces; only all of them show the picture.
abstract.cn: 真相是拼图，facts 是碎片，全找齐才见整图。

examples.en: In fact, the bridge opened two years ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 事实上，大桥提前两年通车。

examples.en: The article mixes fact with speculation.
examples.cn: 这篇文章把事实与猜测混在一起。

examples.en: History books record the facts of the period, not the rumours.
examples.cn: 史书记录那个时代的事实，而非传言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法克特」——法律可证之「特」殊之事，就是事实。

root: 拉丁语 facere（做）的过去分词 factum（已做成之事）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 fact/fait 进入英语。同根词族广大：factory（做的场所）、factor（起作用者）、manufacture（手工做）。

sensesIntro.en: From a deed done outward to known truth, reality, and pieces of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「已做之事」扩展到已知真相、实在与证据条目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing already done, standing there as evidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件已经做完、站在那里作证的事。

branches.en: THE KNOWN: information shown to be true.
branches.cn: 已知之事：被证明为真的信息。

branches.en: THE REAL: truth against invention.
branches.cn: 实在：与虚构相对的真实。

branches.en: THE HAPPENED: the event itself.
branches.cn: 已发生：事件本身。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: details supporting claims.
branches.cn: 证据：支撑论点的细节。

branches.en: THE RECORD: facts kept in writing.
branches.cn: 记录：被写下的事实。

intro.en: Fact is a naked piece of the Latin verb facere; the whole fac- family is around it.
intro.cn: fact 是拉丁动词 facere 裸露的一块；整个 fac- 词族围绕它。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, to do or make, seeds a huge word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere（做、造）孕育了庞大的词族。

definition_zh: 工厂；制造厂
definition_en: a building or organization where goods are manufactured in large quantities
core_image: 流水线上一排机械臂此起彼伏，传送带把零件送进、把成品送出
scene: 参观日，学生戴上安全帽，隔着玻璃看机器人手臂焊接车壳。Through the glass the students watched the robots weld car bodies in the factory.
sceneCN: 这里指「制造商品的场所」，对应第 1 个义项：批量生产货物的建筑；句意为学生隔玻璃观看工厂里机器人焊接车身。画面要点：安全帽、玻璃隔断、机械臂火花。

derivatives.zh: 制造（拉丁 manu「手」加词根 fac「做」，本义手工制作，今指批量生产）
制造业（动词的名词化）
工厂复数（基础词加复数变化）
因素（同根词，指起作用的成分）
轻易的（同根形容词，指容易做到的）

senses.title: A building where goods are made
senses.definition: a large building or group of buildings where goods are manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 批量制造商品的大型建筑或建筑群
senses.example: The factory turns out toys every day.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂每天生产玩具。
senses.why: The place sense grew directly from the Latin 'place of doing'; making goods is just doing, organized.
senses.whyCN: 场所义直接从拉丁语「做事之地」长出；造货就是把「做」组织化。

senses.title: The workers and system of production
senses.definition: the organization and workforce of manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 制造业的组织与劳动力
senses.example: The whole factory stopped for repairs.
senses.why: Once a building means organized making, the word covers the people inside it too.
senses.whyCN: 建筑既指有组织的制作，这个词也顺势涵盖其中的人。

senses.title: A place producing one thing in quantity
senses.definition: any site that produces large amounts of a single product
senses.definitionCN: 大量产出单一产品的地方
senses.example: A data factory of numbers
senses.why: Large-scale single output repeats the factory pattern outside industry.
senses.whyCN: 大规模单一产出把工厂模式复制到了工业之外。

intro.en: Factory comes from Latin factorium, a place where things are done or made.
intro.cn: factory 来自拉丁语 factorium，即做东西或办事的场所。

items.en: Latin factorium meant an oil press or a place of business, from factor, a doer.
items.cn: 拉丁语 factorium 指油坊或事务所，来自 factor（做事者）。

items.en: Medieval Latin factorium named trading posts overseas as well as workshops.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 factorium 也用来称呼海外商站。

items.en: Portuguese feitoria kept the overseas trading-post sense in the age of sail.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 feitoria 在大航海时代保留了海外商站之义。

items.en: French factorerie passed the trading-post sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 factorerie 把商站之义传入英语。

items.en: Modern English settled factory for a building where goods are manufactured by machinery.
items.cn: 现代英语把 factory 固定为用机器批量制造商品的建筑。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root fac-; near-meaning words name places of making.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fac-；近义组命名「制造场所」。

entries.definition: a thing that acts to produce a result
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的因素；同出拉丁 facere

entries.definition: a thing known to be true
entries.definitionCN: 事实；同根不同缀
能力；学院；拼写相近但词源为拉丁 facilitas

entries.definition: a factory, especially for grain or steel
entries.definitionCN: 工厂（多指磨坊、钢铁厂）

entries.definition: a factory for power or heavy industry
entries.definitionCN: 工厂（多指电厂、重工业）

entries.definition: a room or building where manual work is done
entries.definitionCN: 作坊；车间

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for a place of making.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「制作场所」的五个抓手。

normal.en: fact (do) plus -ory (place) adds up to a place where things are made.
normal.cn: fact（做）+ -ory（场所）＝做东西的地方。

normal.en: The plural changes y to i: factories, like cities and stories.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 i：factories，同 cities、stories。

normal.en: car factory and steel factory are everyday pairings in news and traffic.
normal.cn: car factory、steel factory 都是超高频搭配。

normal.en: factory farming means high-density livestock production, common in the papers.
normal.cn: factory farming 指高密度养殖，新闻里常见。

normal.en: factor, fact, and perfect all carry the same Latin verb for doing.
normal.cn: factor、fact、perfect 都含「做」。

abstract.en: A factory is a big standardized box: workers go in, products come out.
abstract.cn: 工厂是把劳动标准化的大盒子：人进去，产品出来。

abstract.en: The assembly line turns time itself into parts, consumed one slot at a time.
abstract.cn: 流水线让时间也变成零件，一格一格被消费。

abstract.en: On every city's edge squat rows of silent giant iron boxes.
abstract.cn: 每个城市的郊区都蹲着一排沉默的巨型铁盒。

examples.en: The chocolate factory smells of cocoa all day.
examples.cn: 巧克力工厂整天飘着可可味。

examples.en: New machines doubled the factory output this year.
examples.cn: 新机器使工厂产量今年翻倍。

examples.en: Her grandfather worked in the factory for thirty years.
examples.cn: 她祖父在这家工厂干了三十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法克特瑞」——法（做）+ 克特（东西）+ 瑞（地方）：做法克东西的地方，就是工厂。

root: 拉丁语 factorium（做事之场所），源自 factor（做事者），后者来自动词 facere（做）。经中世纪拉丁语、葡萄牙语 feitoria 与法语传入英语，词义从商站转移到制造场所。

sensesIntro.en: From a place of doing to the whole system of organized production.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「做事之地」扩展到有组织的生产体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big organized place where raw things go in and finished goods come out.
core.cn: 核心意象：原料进去、成品出来的大型有组织场所。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the building of manufacture.
branches.cn: 场所：制造的建筑。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: people and machines together.
branches.cn: 体系：人与机器的合力。

branches.en: THE SCALE: one product, huge quantity.
branches.cn: 规模：单一产品的大批量。

branches.en: THE ECONOMY: factories as engines of trade.
branches.cn: 经济：工厂作为贸易引擎。

branches.en: THE IMAGE: factory as a metaphor for mindless repetition.
branches.cn: 意象：工厂作为机械重复的隐喻。

intro.en: Factory is fac- (do) plus -ory (place); the suffix family names places and things of doing.
intro.cn: factory 是 fac-（做）加 -ory（场所）；该后缀族命名做事之地与之物。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere gives the root; -ory gives the place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 给出词根；-ory 给出场所。

items.meaning: to make by hand or machine

definition_zh: 失败；不及格；失灵；辜负；缺乏
definition_en: to not succeed, not pass, stop working, disappoint, or be lacking
core_image: 一只伸向目标的手在半空停住，指尖离终点还差一寸
scene: 考试结束铃响，小明放下笔，知道最后一题没答完。The clock rang, and he knew the last question would fail him.
sceneCN: 这里指「未通过、不及格」，对应第 2 个义项：未达到考核标准；句意为铃响时他明白最后一题没写完会让他不及格。画面要点：铃声、摊开的空白试卷、放下的笔。

pos.zh: 失败；不及格；失灵；辜负；缺乏

derivatives.zh: 失败；故障（动词加名词后缀，指失败这件事或失灵之物）
缺点；弱点（现在分词转名词，指性格上的欠缺）
可靠不衰的（否定前缀加现在分词形容词，指从不落空）
防故障的（复合形容词，指失手也不会酿灾）

senses.title: To not succeed
senses.definition: to not achieve what was attempted
senses.definitionCN: 未能达成所谋之事
senses.example: They failed to reach the summit.
senses.why: The core image is falling short of a goal; the attempt simply comes up empty.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是够不着目标；尝试最终落空。

senses.title: To not pass a test
senses.definition: to not reach the required standard in a test or course
senses.definitionCN: 在测试或课程中未达标
senses.example: He failed the driving test.
senses.why: A standard is a goal; missing it is the same falling short in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 标准即目标；差之毫厘同属「够不着」。

senses.title: To stop working properly
senses.definition: to stop working, or to become weaker
senses.definitionCN: 停止正常运作，或变得衰弱
senses.example: The engine failed in mid-air.
senses.why: A tool that disappoints its user has 'deceived' them; machines fail like false friends.
senses.whyCN: 让使用者失望的工具就是「欺骗」了他们；机器像假朋友一样 fail。

senses.title: To let someone down
senses.definition: to not give someone the help or result they hoped for
senses.definitionCN: 未能给予对方所期望的帮助或结果
senses.example: His memory failed him at the exam.
senses.why: The root meaning 'deceive' survives here: hoping and not receiving.
senses.whyCN: 词根「欺骗」之义在此存留：期望落空。

senses.title: To be absent or in short supply
senses.definition: to not be present or available when needed
senses.definitionCN: 需要时不在场或不可得
senses.example: The rains failed that year.
senses.why: What is missing has, in old French eyes, 'fallen short'; lack is a kind of falling.
senses.whyCN: 在古法语视角里，缺失即「落空」；匮乏是一种跌落。

intro.en: Fail goes back to Latin fallere, 'to deceive or disappoint'; to fail someone is to let their hope fall through.
intro.cn: fail 回溯拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、令人失望）；使某人 fail 就是让其落空。

items.en: Latin fallere meant to deceive; its intransitive use gave 'to be lacking, disappoint'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 意为欺骗；其不及物用法给出「缺失、落空」。

items.en: Old French faillir meant to be lacking, to miss, and grew into falir.
items.cn: 古法语 faillir 意为缺失、未做到。

items.en: Anglo-French failir, failer carried the sense of falling short into England.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语 failir、failer 把「不足」之义带入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English failen meant to be deficient, to miscarry, to not succeed.
items.cn: 中古英语 failen 意为欠缺、失败、不成功。

items.en: Modern English added the school sense 'to not pass a test' and the noun failure family.
items.cn: 现代英语增加「考试不及格」之义并衍生 failure 一族。

note.en: Look-alikes share spelling or the Latin root fall-; near-meaning words live in the field of not succeeding.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写或拉丁词根 fall-；近义组处于「未成功」的义场。

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for disappointing.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「令人落空」之词的五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin fallere means to deceive or let down, so fail is a hope falling through.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fallere＝欺骗、落空；fail 就是让希望落空。

normal.en: fail to do something is the all-purpose pattern for not managing an action.
normal.cn: fail to do sth 是万能句型：没能做某事。

normal.en: without fail means always, a regular guest at the end of polite letters.
normal.cn: without fail 意为「务必」，信件结尾常客。

normal.en: the noun failure covers both defeat and breakdown, and exams love it.
normal.cn: failure 名词，考纲高频，既是失败也是故障。

normal.en: fail, false, and fault are cousins: all about trickery and empty hands.
normal.cn: fail 与 false、fault 同根，都是「骗与空」。

abstract.en: Failure is a letter sent with no reply, addressed to yourself.
abstract.cn: 失败是一封没有回音的信，收件人是自己。

abstract.en: A pass mark is a bar drawn above your head; failing means never clearing it.
abstract.cn: 不及格是标准线在你头顶画的一道横杠，你没跳过去。

abstract.en: A machine failing feels like a friend missing an appointment: the promised thing simply vanishes.
abstract.cn: 机器失灵像朋友失约：说好的事突然没了。

examples.en: Without fail, the early bus arrives at seven every morning.
examples.cn: 早班车每天早上七点准时到，从不例外。

examples.en: She failed her first driving test but passed the second.
examples.cn: 她第一次驾照考试没过，第二次通过了。

examples.en: The old bridge failed under the heavy truck.
examples.cn: 旧桥在重型卡车下垮了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费哦」——费了半天劲结果哦一声落空，就是 fail。

root: 拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、令人落空）经古法语 faillir 与盎格鲁法语 failir 进入英语。同根词 false（假）、fault（过错）都保留「欺骗」的底色；fail 的各种义项都围绕「落空」展开。

sensesIntro.en: From falling short of a goal outward to tests, machines, people, and scarcity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「够不着目标」扩展到考试、机器、他人与匮乏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reaching for something and not getting it.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去够，却没有够到。

branches.en: THE GOAL MISSED: effort without success.
branches.cn: 未达之标：努力而无成。

branches.en: THE BAR MISSED: not reaching a standard.
branches.cn: 未越之杠：未达标准。

branches.en: THE BROKEN TOOL: machines that stop.
branches.cn: 失灵之器：停摆的机器。

branches.en: THE BROKEN PROMISE: people who disappoint.
branches.cn: 落空的期待：令人失望之人。

branches.en: THE EMPTY HAND: things that are lacking.
branches.cn: 空手：匮乏之物。

intro.en: Fail is the bare French face of the Latin root fall- (deceive); its family is all about trickery and falling short.
intro.cn: fail 是拉丁词根 fall-（欺骗）的法语素颜形态；词族围绕「骗与落空」。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere, to deceive, seeds false, fault, and fail.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 孕育 false、fault 与 fail。

items.exampleCN: failure 既指失败也指故障

definition_zh: 公平的；公正的；按规则行事的；浅色的；晴朗的；尚可的；相当多的；（旧）美丽的；（名词）集市、交易会
definition_en: treating people equally and following the rules, and, by older widening, light in colour, clear in weather, moderate in degree, handsome in appearance, or a gathering where goods are traded
core_image: 一架天平两端放着同样的砝码，指针停在正中，旁边摊开的规则手册对双方写着一模一样的条款
scene: 裁判在中线把球权判给先触球的一方，双方队员都照同一份规则手册行事。The referee awarded the ball to the side that touched it first, and both teams played a fair game.
sceneCN: 这里指「按共同规则行事、不偏袒任何一方」，对应第 2 个义项：在竞赛或交易中依照事先约定的规则而不取巧；句意为裁判把球权判给先触球的一方，两队都按规则比赛。画面要点：中线、裁判手势、两队球衣、摊开的规则手册。

pos.zh: 公平的；公正的；按规则的；浅色的；晴朗的；尚可的；相当多的；（旧）美丽的
集市；交易会；博览会（另出一源，与形容词不同源）
公平地；按规则地（常用于表示按规则做事的固定说法）

collocations.zh: 公平的交易；公正的待遇

derivatives.zh: 公平；公正（基础词加古英语表性质的名词后缀，由形容词转为抽象状态）
公平地；相当地（基础词加副词后缀，语义由「公正」扩展到「程度适中」）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词，指偏离规则或偏袒一方）
公正的；不偏不倚的（基础词与「心智」一词加过去分词后缀构成的复合形容词，指判断不受私利影响）
集市或博览会的场地（基础词与「地面」一词构成的复合名词，语义由交易会转向其举办场所）

senses.title: Even-handed in judgment
senses.titleCN: 判断时不偏袒任何一方
senses.definition: treating people equally and not letting personal preference decide an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 平等待人，不让个人好恶决定结果
senses.example: A fair judge hears both sides before ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 公正的法官在裁决前会听取双方陈述。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the word was 'beautiful, clean'; an unblemished decision was felt as something clean and pleasing, so the idea of even-handedness grew out of that older picture rather than from a word for law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思是「美好的、洁净的」；不受污染的裁决被感受为洁净而令人愉悦之物，因此「公正」义是从那幅旧图景长出来的，而不是来自某个表示法律的词。

senses.title: According to the agreed rules
senses.titleCN: 依照事先约定的规则行事
senses.definition: played or done in the way the rules require, without trickery or advantage taken
senses.definitionCN: 按照规则要求去做，不取巧、不占便宜
senses.example: The referee awarded the ball to the side that touched it first, and both teams played a fair game.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判把球权判给先触球的一方，两队都按规则比赛。
senses.why: Once equal treatment is expected between opponents, the word names the conduct that keeps the contest equal, which is why sport fixed the phrase fair play.
senses.whyCN: 当对手之间被期待受到同等对待，这个词就用来指维持竞赛对等的行为，体育因此固定下「公平竞赛」这一说法。

senses.title: Light in colour
senses.definition: pale or light in colour, especially of hair, skin or cloth
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浅淡，尤指头发、皮肤或织物
senses.example: The child had fair hair and a sunburned nose.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子头发浅淡，鼻子晒得发红。
senses.why: A clean, bright appearance was the core of the old sense, and lightness of colour is exactly what that brightness looks like on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 洁净明亮的外观是旧义的核心，而颜色的浅淡正是这种明亮落在表面上的样子。

senses.title: Clear and cloudless weather
senses.definition: bright and dry, with no rain and little cloud
senses.definitionCN: 明亮干燥、无雨少云
senses.example: The forecast promised fair weather for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说渡海期间天气晴好。
senses.why: A sky without cloud shares the same visual core of brightness and cleanliness, so the weather sense needs no separate origin.
senses.whyCN: 无云的天空共享同一个明亮洁净的视觉核心，因此天气义无需另找来源。

senses.title: Moderately good, no more
senses.definition: acceptable but not excellent; average in quality
senses.definitionCN: 可以接受但不算出色；质量中等
senses.example: The hotel was fair, neither luxurious nor shabby.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆还算可以，既不豪华也不破旧。
senses.why: In grading, 'pleasing enough' slid downward from praise to mere adequacy, and the old phrase fair to middling fixed the middling reading.
senses.whyCN: 在评级中，「足够令人满意」从称赞滑向仅仅及格，旧说法「尚可、中不溜」把这种中等义固定了下来。

senses.title: Considerable in size or amount
senses.definition: large enough to be worth noticing, though not stated exactly
senses.definitionCN: 大到值得注意，但没有确切说出数量
senses.example: A fair number of students stayed after class to ask questions.
senses.exampleCN: 相当多的学生下课后留下来提问。
senses.why: The 'handsome, ample' reading came from the sense of something fine and substantial, not from justice, which is why a fair amount can be large without being equal.
senses.whyCN: 「可观、充足」这一读法来自「美好而结实」的意思，与公正无关；所以「相当多的量」可以很大，却与平等无关。

senses.title: Beautiful, in older use
senses.definition: lovely to look at, used of women in older literature and ballads
senses.definitionCN: 容貌秀美，旧文学与民谣中用于形容女子
senses.example: The fair maiden in the old ballad waited by the well.
senses.exampleCN: 古老民谣里那位美丽的少女在井边等候。
senses.why: This is the earliest recorded sense and the source of all the others; it survives in fixed literary phrases rather than in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最早义项，也是其余义项的源头；它只残留在固定的文学说法里，不再用于日常口语。

senses.title: A gathering where goods are traded
senses.titleCN: 集市、交易会（名词，另出一源）
senses.definition: a large outdoor or indoor event where stalls and companies show and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 在户外或室内举办、由摊位与公司展示并销售商品的大型活动
senses.example: Farmers brought wool and cheese to the annual fair.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把羊毛和奶酪带到一年一度的集市上。
senses.why: The noun is a different word: Latin feria 'festival day' came through Old French and fell together with the adjective in spelling, so the market sense has no link to justice.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是另一个词：拉丁语中意为「节日」的词经古法语传入，拼写上才与形容词合流，因此集市义与公正义并无牵连。

intro.en: Fair as an adjective comes from Old English fæger 'beautiful, pleasant, clean', a Germanic word with recorded relatives in Gothic. The noun for a market is a separate borrowing from Latin feria 'festival day'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 作形容词的 fair 来自古英语 fæger「美好的、愉悦的、洁净的」，属日耳曼语词，哥特语中有可考的同族形式。作「集市」解的名词另出拉丁 feria「节日」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fæger meant 'beautiful, pleasant, clean' and was applied to people, weather, land and objects alike. All the later senses grow from this single descriptive word.
items.cn: fæger 意为「美好的、愉悦的、洁净的」，可用于人、天气、土地与器物。后来各义项都从这一个描写性词生长出来。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form *fagraz is posited as the common ancestor; Gothic fagrs 'fitting, suitable' is its closest recorded relative. The starred form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 学界拟构的日耳曼语形式 *fagraz 被推为共同祖先；哥特语 fagrs「合适的、相称的」是它最近的可考同族词。带星号的形式属重构形式，并非有文献实证的词。

items.en: Source uncertain: no accepted Indo-European ancestor is established for the Germanic adjective. A connection with a root meaning 'to make beautiful' has been suggested, but it remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个日耳曼形容词尚无公认的印欧语祖先。有人提出它与一个意为「使美」的词根相关，但那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: By the Middle English period the word described decisions and dealings that were clean of bias, and this equitable sense became the dominant everyday one.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，这个词已用来描述不带偏私的裁决与交易，这一公正义随后成为日常使用中的主导义。

items.en: Light hair and cloudless skies were both called fair because both shared the old core of clean brightness; neither sense required a new source.
items.cn: 浅色的头发与无云的天空都被称作 fair，因为两者都共享「洁净明亮」这一旧核心；这两个义项都不需要新的来源。

items.en: The market noun descends from Latin feria 'festival day', through Old French feire. It is homonymous with the adjective only in modern spelling; the two words are unrelated at the root.
items.cn: 「集市」这一名词出自拉丁 feria「节日」，经古法语 feire 传入。它只在现代拼写上与形容词同形；两个词在词根上并无关联。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes and homophones that are constantly mistaken for this word; the second group holds near alternatives for the idea of even-handedness.
note.cn: 第一组是极易与这个词混淆的形近词与同音词；第二组是「不偏不倚」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: The money paid for a journey, or food provided; it comes from an Old English word for a journey, not from the adjective for beauty or justice.
entries.definitionCN: 旅费或供应的饮食；出自古英语中表示「行程」的词，与表示美好或公正的形容词无关。

entries.definition: A small magical being; the word comes from Old French faerie 'enchantment', so the resemblance to fair is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小巧的魔法生灵；该词出自古法语中表示「魔法、魅惑」的词，因此与「美好」一词的相似只是巧合。

entries.definition: The adverb of fair, but it splits into 'in a just manner' and 'to a moderate degree', the second being far more common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 这是该形容词的副词形式，但分成「以公正的方式」与「达到中等程度」两读，后者在口语中常见得多。

entries.definition: A deliberately archaic spelling of the market noun, used by organisers to suggest a traditional festival; it adds no new meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 「集市」这一名词故意仿古的拼法，主办方用它暗示传统节庆；并不增添新义。

entries.definition: Conforming to what is morally right or lawful; it judges the outcome, while fair stresses the equal treatment that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 符合道德上正确或法律上正当的要求；它评判结果，而本词更强调产生结果时的平等待遇。

entries.definition: Fair in a formal or legal setting, often correcting a strict rule to reach a balanced result; it is the technical counterpart of the plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 在正式或法律语境中表示公平，常用来修正过严的规则以取得平衡结果；它是较朴素那个词的专业对应词。

entries.definition: Not favouring one party over another; it describes the absence of bias, whereas fair can also praise a positive even-handedness.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方；它描述的是没有偏见，而本词还可称赞一种积极的持平态度。

entries.definition: Light in colour, often suggesting less brightness than normal; it covers one sense of fair but never carries judgment or weather.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色浅，常暗示比正常情况少了些血色或亮度；它只覆盖其中一个义项，从不带判断或天气之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the recorded Old English sense, real derived words and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：有文献可考的古英语义项、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The oldest sense is 'beautiful, clean', so a fair decision is pictured as an unblemished surface.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是「美好的、洁净的」，因此公正的裁决被想象成一块没有污点的表面。

normal.en: The family runs fair, fairly, fairness, unfair, fair-minded and fairground.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词及其副词形式、表性质的名词、否定形式与复合形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: fair play, fair weather, fair hair, a fair amount, a trade fair.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把各义项分开：公平竞赛、晴朗天气、浅色头发、相当多的量、贸易博览会。

normal.en: Fare, the price of a journey, sounds identical but belongs to a different Old English word.
normal.cn: 表示旅费的另一个同音词读音完全相同，却属于另一个古英语词。

normal.en: The market noun came from Latin feria 'festival day', so a county fair and a fair judgment are unrelated at the root.
normal.cn: 表示集市的名词出自拉丁语中意为「节日」的词，因此乡村集市与公正裁决在词根上毫不相干。

abstract.en: Picture a balance whose two pans carry different weights but whose beam stays level because the rulebook sits on the fulcrum.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两只托盘放着不同的重量，横梁却保持水平，因为规则手册就垫在支点上。

abstract.en: Picture a white sky over a pale field, the same brightness spread across weather, hair and cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象苍白田野上方的白色天空，同一种明亮铺在天气、头发与布料上。

abstract.en: Picture two separate rivers that happen to join at one estuary: one carries an old song, the other a holiday crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象两条本不相干的河流恰在同一河口汇合：一条载着古老的歌，一条载着过节的人群。

examples.en: The committee reached a fair settlement that both sides could accept.
examples.cn: 委员会达成了一个双方都能接受的公平和解。

examples.en: Fair weather held until the boats were halfway across the bay.
examples.cn: 晴好的天气一直持续到船只驶过海湾中段。

examples.en: She keeps a fair number of old maps in the bottom drawer.
examples.cn: 她在最下面的抽屉里存着相当多的旧地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费厄」——费厄泼赖就是按规则公平竞赛，凡事照同一本规则来 → 公平的、按规则的

root: 古英语 fæger「美好的、洁净的」，与哥特语 fagrs「相称的」同族；更深来源不确定，有「使美」词根的假说，属重构形式。名词「集市」义另出拉丁 feria「节日」，经古法语 feire 借入，与形容词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one picture: a surface that is clean and bright. That brightness becomes light colour, then clear weather, then a beautiful person, then a decision with no stain on it. From the unstained decision come rule-bound play, mere adequacy and a sizeable amount, while the market sense enters English by a separate Latin road.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一幅图景展开：一块洁净明亮的表面。这种明亮先成为浅色，再成为晴朗，再成为美丽的容貌，再成为没有污点的裁决。从无污点的裁决又分出依规则行事、仅够及格与数量可观；而集市义则沿着另一条拉丁语道路进入英语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean, bright surface on which no stain or tilt can be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块洁净明亮的表面，看不出任何污点或倾斜。

branches.en: UNSTAINED JUDGMENT: the ethical reading, where no personal preference leaves a mark on the outcome.
branches.cn: 无污点的判断：伦理层面的读法，个人好恶不在结果上留下痕迹。

branches.en: RULES AND ADEQUACY: equal conduct between opponents, and the milder reading of 'good enough' that grading produced.
branches.cn: 规则与及格：对手之间的对等行为，以及评级产生的「还算可以」这一较弱读法。

branches.en: BRIGHTNESS ON A SURFACE: light hair and cloudless sky are the old brightness seen outdoors and on a body.
branches.cn: 表面上的明亮：浅色头发与无云天空，是那种旧有的明亮落在户外与人身上。

branches.en: AMPLE AND LOVELY: a handsome size, and the oldest literary sense of beauty that started the whole family.
branches.cn: 充足与秀美：可观的规模，以及开启整个词族的最早文学义「美」。

branches.en: SEPARATE MARKET WORD: a festival day borrowed from Latin, joined only by spelling.
branches.cn: 另源的集市词：从拉丁语借来的节日，只靠拼写与前者合流。

intro.en: Fair is a native English adjective whose endings are Germanic, while the market noun arrived separately from Latin, so the family carries two unrelated histories.
intro.cn: 该词是英语本族的形容词，其词尾属日耳曼语；而表示集市的名词另从拉丁语传入，因此这个词族携带两段互不相干的历史。

latinIntro.en: The adjective has no Latin source. The Latin forms below belong only to the market noun, and the Latin word for a festival day is not related to the adjective for beauty or justice.
latinIntro.cn: 这个形容词没有拉丁语来源。下列拉丁形式只属于表示集市的名词；拉丁语中表示节日的词，与表示美或公正的形容词并无关联。

items.example: Both teams played a fair game.
The review questioned the fairness of the test.
items.exampleCN: 评审质疑这项测试的公平性。

items.example: It was unfair to single out one applicant.
items.exampleCN: 单独挑出一名申请者是不公平的。

items.meaningCN: 愿意不带偏见地判断的
items.example: A fair-minded reader will check the sources.
items.exampleCN: 公正的读者会去核对来源。

items.meaning: the site of a market or show
items.example: Trucks queued at the gate of the fairground.
items.exampleCN: 卡车在集市场地门口排队。

items.meaning: loyal only while things go well
items.example: A fair-weather ally left when the storm came.
items.exampleCN: 一个只能同甘的盟友在风暴来时就离开了。

items.example: The coach praised the visiting side for its fair play.
items.exampleCN: 教练称赞客队遵守规则。

items.structure: fayre (revived spelling of the market noun)
items.meaningCN: 仿古拼写的集市或节庆
items.example: The village held a summer fayre on the green.
items.exampleCN: 村子在草地上举办了夏季集市。

derivatives.zh: 公平；公正（基础词加表性质的名词后缀，由形容词转为抽象状态）
公正地；相当地（基础词加副词后缀，语义扩展到程度适中）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词，指偏袒或违背规则）
公正的（基础词与「心智」复合再加分词后缀，指判断不受私利左右）

definition_zh: 相当地；还算；公正地；按规则地；（旧）完全地
definition_en: to a moderate degree, or in a just and rule-abiding manner
core_image: 一根指针停在刻度盘正中偏左：既不到顶，也不落底，读数刚好可以接受
scene: 试镜结束后评委低声交换意见，认为这位新人的表现中规中矩。The judges agreed that the newcomer sang fairly well.
sceneCN: 这里指「相当地、还算」，对应第 1 个义项：程度适中但不夸张；句意为评委一致认为新人唱得还不错。画面要点：评委席、低声耳语、打分表。

derivatives.zh: 公平的；晴朗的（基础形容词，fairly 的词源）
公平（形容词加名词后缀，指公正的性质）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词）
不公平地（否定前缀加副词后缀）

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: to some extent, but not very
senses.definitionCN: 在某种程度上，但并不非常
senses.example: The film was fairly good.
senses.why: The old sense 'pleasing enough' slid from praise into moderation, and the adverb inherited that milder reading.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「还算令人满意」从称赞滑向中等，副词继承了这一较弱的读法。

senses.title: In a just manner
senses.definition: honestly and according to the rules
senses.definitionCN: 诚实地、按规则地
senses.example: Both teams played fairly.
senses.why: The adverb first walked beside the adjective: a fair deed done fairly keeps the same clean surface.
senses.whyCN: 副词最初紧随形容词：公正之事以公正之姿完成，保持同一洁净表面。

senses.title: Completely, in older use
senses.definition: used before adjectives of absolute meaning to mean quite or entirely
senses.definitionCN: 用于绝对意义形容词之前，意为相当、完全
senses.example: The old wall was fairly ruined.
senses.exampleCN: 那堵旧墙几乎完全塌了。
senses.why: Before absolute adjectives the degree reading stretches to the far end: quite, entirely.
senses.whyCN: 置于绝对形容词前时，程度义被拉到另一端：相当、完全。

intro.en: Fairly is simply the adverb of fair: the Old English adjective fair gained the Germanic adverb ending -ly, and its meaning split into 'justly' and 'moderately'.
intro.cn: fairly 就是 fair 的副词形式：古英语形容词 fair 加上日耳曼副词词尾 -ly，词义随后分裂为「公正地」与「相当地」。

items.en: Old English fæger 'beautiful, clean' already formed adverbs with endings meaning 'in a fair manner'.
items.cn: 古英语 fæger「美好、洁净」已能用副词词尾构成「以公正方式」之类的副词。

items.en: Middle English used faireliche and fairly for 'beautifully' and 'justly', both close to the adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语用 faireliche、fairly 表示「美丽地」「公正地」，都与形容词贴近。

items.en: Early Modern English kept 'justly' as the main reading in phrases like play fairly.
items.cn: 早期现代英语保留「公正地」为主要读法，如 play fairly。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the degree reading 'to a moderate extent' took over, especially before adjectives.
items.cn: 十九世纪「达到中等程度」的读法占了上风，尤用于形容词之前。

items.en: Modern English fairly before an adjective or adverb almost always softens it: fairly good, fairly quickly.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fairly 置于形容词或副词前几乎总是缓和语气：fairly good、fairly quickly。

note.en: Look-alikes share the -ly adverb ending or the fair stem; near-meaning words soften or measure degree.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ly 副词词尾或 fair 词干；近义组用于缓和语气或度量程度。

entries.definition: the adjective fair itself; fairly is its adverb
entries.definitionCN: 形容词 fair 本身；fairly 是它的副词

entries.definition: a small magical being; sounds identical
entries.definitionCN: 小仙子；发音完全相同，词源无关
旅费；同音异义，源自「行程」一词

entries.definition: to a moderate or surprising degree
entries.definitionCN: 相当；有点（语气略强于 fairly）

entries.definition: to some degree; completely in British use
entries.definitionCN: 相当；在英国英语中可指完全

entries.definition: in a fair and right manner
entries.definitionCN: 公正地；仅覆盖公正一义

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a small adverb that both softens and judges.
normalIntro.cn: 既能缓和语气又能评判公正的小副词，五个抓手。

normal.en: fairly is fair plus -ly, so its two readings both descend from the adjective.
normal.cn: fairly＝fair+-ly，两个读法都从形容词降下来。

normal.en: Before an adjective it usually means 'quite but not very': fairly good is less than very good.
normal.cn: 置于形容词前通常表示「还算但非非常」：fairly good 弱于 very good。

normal.en: play fair and play fairly mean the same thing in sport.
normal.cn: play fair 与 play fairly 在体育里意思相同。

normal.en: rather is stronger than fairly, and quite can be stronger still in British English.
normal.cn: rather 比 fairly 语气强，英国英语里 quite 可更强。

normal.en: The fairy homophone has nothing to do with justice.
normal.cn: 同音词 fairy（仙子）与公正毫无关系。

abstract.en: Moderation is a mid-mark on a ruler: fairly points at it with a steady finger.
abstract.cn: 适中是尺子上的中点刻度：fairly 用手指稳稳点在上面。

abstract.en: A just act needs no tilt; fairly describes a beam that stays level.
abstract.cn: 公正之行无需倾斜；fairly 描述的是保持水平的横梁。

abstract.en: Softeners are the polite grammar of honesty: fairly admits a truth without shouting it.
abstract.cn: 缓和词是诚实的礼貌语法：fairly 承认真相但不喊出来。

examples.en: The instructions were fairly clear, so we finished quickly.
examples.cn: 说明还算清楚，所以我们很快做完了。

examples.en: Referees must treat both sides fairly.
examples.cn: 裁判必须公平对待双方。

examples.en: The journey took fairly long because of the snow.
examples.cn: 因为下雪，旅程花了相当长的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费尔利」——费尔（fair）之后加「利」落，公平办利索事 → 公正地、相当地。

root: fair（古英语 fæger「美好、洁净」）加日耳曼副词词尾 -ly 构成。原义「公正地、美丽地」，十九世纪起「相当地」的程度用法成为主导。

sensesIntro.en: From the adverb of fairness outward to moderate degree and old absolute use.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「公正」的副词形式扩展到中等程度义与旧的绝对用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting at the middle of the scale, neither maxed nor empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在刻度中段，既不满格也不空格。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: quite, but not very.
branches.cn: 程度：相当，但非非常。

branches.en: THE JUSTNESS: acting without bias.
branches.cn: 公正：行事不带偏私。

branches.en: THE OLD READING: entirely, before absolute adjectives.
branches.cn: 旧读法：置于绝对形容词前表完全。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: moderation as the everyday face of fairness.
branches.cn: 平衡：中庸是公正的日常面孔。

branches.en: THE SLIDER: one adverb covering both ends of the scale.
branches.cn: 滑杆：一个副词覆盖刻度两端。

intro.en: Fairly is built with the plain Germanic adverb ending; its family is the whole fair word-tree.
intro.cn: fairly 由朴素的日耳曼副词词尾构成；词族即整个 fair 词树。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin member in this family; all forms are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有拉丁成员；所有形式都是日耳曼语。

items.example: quickly means in a quick manner
the fairness of the test was questioned
items.exampleCN: 测试的公正性受到质疑

items.example: Fair enough, you win this round.

definition_zh: 落下；跌倒；下降；沦陷；秋季（名词）；瀑布
definition_en: to drop downward, decline, be defeated, or pass into a state; also the season of autumn
core_image: 一片叶子从枝头脱手，沿一条看不见的斜线滑向地面，中途没有东西接住它
scene: 上课铃响后老师走进教室，喧闹声一点一点沉下去。When the teacher entered, the room fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里指「进入某种状态」，对应第 5 个义项：落入寂静；句意为老师进教室后房间安静下来。画面要点：门口的身影、渐渐停下的嗡嗡声、翻开的书本。

derivatives.zh: 下降的（现在分词作形容词）
倒下的；凋落的（过去分词作形容词，如 fallen leaves）
瀑布（复合名词：水之落差）
黄昏（复合名词：夜之来临）
降雨量（复合名词：雨之降落量）

senses.title: To drop downward
senses.definition: to move downward, usually quickly and without control
senses.definitionCN: 通常快速且失控地向下运动
senses.example: An apple fell from the tree.
senses.why: Gravity is the first teacher of the word: things let go go down.
senses.whyCN: 重力是这个词的第一位老师：松手之物向下。

senses.title: To come down from standing
senses.definition: to lose balance and end on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 失去平衡倒在地上
senses.example: She slipped and fell on the ice.
senses.why: Standing is the human default; losing it is falling even on flat ground.
senses.whyCN: 站立是人的默认状态；失去它即是跌倒，哪怕在平地上。

senses.title: To decrease or decline
senses.definition: to become lower in amount, level or value
senses.definitionCN: 数量、水平或价值变低
senses.example: Prices fell sharply last month.
senses.why: What drops in space also drops in number: the vertical map becomes a chart.
senses.whyCN: 空间中的下落在数量中同样成立：垂直的地图变成图表。

senses.title: To be defeated or captured
senses.definition: to be taken by an enemy, as a city or government
senses.definitionCN: （城市、政府等）被敌方攻占
senses.example: The city fell after a long siege.
senses.exampleCN: 围城很久之后城市陷落。
senses.why: A standing wall or regime that comes down is a fall on the scale of history.
senses.whyCN: 屹立的城墙或政权倒下，就是历史尺度上的 fall。

senses.title: To pass into a state or place
senses.definition: to move into a condition, silence, or someone's hands
senses.definitionCN: 进入某种状态、寂静，或落入他人之手
senses.example: The room fell silent.
senses.why: Landing somewhere is arriving in some state: the ground maps onto the condition.
senses.whyCN: 落到某处即进入某状态：地面被映射为境况。

intro.en: Fall is one of the oldest strong verbs in English, going straight back to a Germanic root for dropping down.
intro.cn: fall 是英语最古老的强变化动词之一，直接回溯到日耳曼语表「落下」的词根。

items.en: The reconstructed root fallan meant to fall or drop down; Gothic and Old Norse show the same verb.
items.cn: 重构词根 fallan 意为落下；哥特语与古诺斯语显示同一动词。

items.en: Old English feallan kept the strong conjugation: feoll for the past.
items.cn: 古英语 feallan 保留强变化：过去式 feoll。

items.en: Norse falla reinforced the verb in northern England and gave the noun fall 'a drop, a decline'.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 falla 在英格兰北方加固该动词，并给出名词 fall「降落、衰退」。

items.en: Middle English fell/fallen settled the modern conjugation, and the noun expanded to waterfall and nightfall.
items.cn: 中古英语 fell/fallen 确立现代变位，名词扩展出 waterfall、nightfall。

items.en: Modern English added senses of defeat, capture and seasons: fall of a city, the fall of the year.
items.cn: 现代英语增加败落、陷落与季节义：城市陷落、秋季。

note.en: Look-alikes share spelling or the false/fail stem; near-meaning words name kinds of downward movement and defeat.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写或 false/fail 词根；近义组命名各种下落与败落。

entries.definition: to not succeed; from Latin fallere
entries.definitionCN: 失败；源自拉丁 fallere，与 fall 不同源
虚假的；拼写相近，词根为拉丁 fall-

entries.definition: the past of fall, also a verb meaning to cut down
entries.definitionCN: fall 的过去式；另作动词「砍倒」

entries.definition: to fall or let fall a short distance
entries.definitionCN: 落下；坠落（距离较短）

entries.definition: to fall with rolling or uncontrolled movement
entries.definitionCN: 翻滚着跌落

entries.definition: to become gradually lower or weaker
entries.definitionCN: 下降；衰退（趋势性）

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the oldest Germanic word for going down.
normalIntro.cn: 日耳曼语最古老的「向下」之词，五个抓手。

normal.en: fall is a strong verb: fall–fell–fallen, like sing–sang–sung.
normal.cn: fall 是强变化动词：fall–fell–fallen，同 sing–sang–sung。

normal.en: fall asleep, fall in love, fall behind: states you land in like ground.
normal.cn: fall asleep、fall in love、fall behind：像落地一样进入的状态。

normal.en: The season autumn is called the fall in American English, from the fall of leaves.
normal.cn: 美国英语把秋天叫 the fall，源于叶落。

normal.en: Prices fall on charts the same way apples fall from trees.
normal.cn: 图表上的价格下跌与苹果落地是同一个动作。

normal.en: A city that falls in war comes down like a wall.
normal.cn: 战争中被攻陷的城市像墙一样倒下。

abstract.en: Every fall is a conversation between weight and the ground.
abstract.cn: 每一次坠落都是重量与大地的一次对话。

abstract.en: Decline is falling drawn as a line on paper.
abstract.cn: 衰退是画在纸上的下落。

abstract.en: Silence falls into a room like snow falling into a valley.
abstract.cn: 寂静落入房间，像雪落入山谷。

examples.en: The leaves fall every October and cover the lawn.
examples.cn: 叶子每年十月落下，铺满草坪。

examples.en: He fell asleep during the long lecture.
examples.cn: 他在冗长的讲座中睡着了。

examples.en: The old empire fell in a single winter.
examples.cn: 古老的帝国在一个冬天里倾覆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福奥」——福到了头就往下落，fall 就是「落下」。

root: 原始日耳曼语词根 fallan（落下）直接进入古英语 feallan，强变化（fall–fell–fallen）。古诺斯语 falla 加固了北方用法并给出名词义。词义由垂直下落扩展到跌倒、下降、沦陷与状态转变。

sensesIntro.en: From physical dropping outward to stumbling, declining, defeat, and entering new states.
sensesIntro.cn: 从物理性的下落扩展到跌倒、衰退、陷落与进入新状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something let go, moving down until the ground stops it.
core.cn: 核心意象：脱手之物向下运动，直到被地面截住。

branches.en: THE DROP: motion pulled downward.
branches.cn: 坠落：被拉向下方之运动。

branches.en: THE STUMBLE: a body meeting the ground.
branches.cn: 跌倒：身体与大地相遇。

branches.en: THE CURVE: numbers going down.
branches.cn: 曲线：数字下降。

branches.en: THE CAPTURE: a city or regime coming down.
branches.cn: 陷落：城市或政权的倒塌。

branches.en: THE LANDING: arriving in silence, sleep, or hands.
branches.cn: 落定：进入寂静、睡眠或他人之手。

intro.en: Fall is a bare Germanic verb; its family grows by compounding, not by affixing.
intro.cn: fall 是裸的日耳曼动词；词族靠复合而非加缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no member of this Germanic family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这个日耳曼词族中没有成员。

items.example: the fallen leaves covered the path

items.exampleCN: 我们黄昏时分抵达营地

items.meaning: the amount of rain that falls

items.example: the junior staff was the fall guy

definition_zh: 名声；声誉；名气
definition_en: the state of being known or talked about by many people, especially for achievement
core_image: 一座聚光灯下的讲台，台上人的一句话被成千上万张嘴传开
scene: 颁奖礼上主持人宣布得主，全场起立鼓掌，闪光灯连成一片。Winning the prize brought her fame overnight.
sceneCN: 这里指「名声」，对应第 1 个义项：被许多人谈论的状态；句意为获奖让她一夜成名。画面要点：奖杯、闪光灯、起立鼓掌的人群。

collocations.zh: 成名之事；值得一提之处

derivatives.zh: 著名的（同根形容词：被许多人谈论的）
声名狼藉的（否定前缀 in- 加同根词，坏的那半名声）
恶名（同根名词，指坏名声）
诽谤（前缀 de- 加词根 fam-，把名声说坏）
有名的（过去分词作形容词）

senses.title: The state of being widely known
senses.definition: the condition of being known or talked about by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被许多人知晓或谈论的状态
senses.example: She achieved fame at twenty.
senses.why: To be spoken of by many is to exist in many mouths; the root meant exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 被众人谈论即活在众人之口；词根本义正是如此。

senses.title: A good public reputation
senses.definition: a positive reputation for achievement or quality
senses.definitionCN: 因成就或品质而得的正面名声
senses.example: The town won fame for its pottery.
senses.why: Rumor splits: what is said can be praise; the good half is fame.
senses.whyCN: 传闻会分裂：所言可为赞美；好的那一半即声望。

senses.title: Renown in a field or era
senses.titleCN: 某一领域或时代的盛名
senses.definition: lasting recognition within a profession or period
senses.definitionCN: 在某一行业或时期获得的持久认可
senses.example: His fame rests on three novels.
senses.exampleCN: 他的盛名建立在三部小说之上。
senses.why: Recognition that outlives the moment is fame with a long tail.
senses.whyCN: 超越一时的认可即带着长尾的 fame。

intro.en: Fame comes from Latin fama, 'what people say', the same root that gives famous and infamy.
intro.cn: fame 来自拉丁语 fama「人们所说的」，与 famous、infamy 同根。

items.en: Latin fama meant report, rumor, and public opinion; fari meant to speak.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fama 意为传闻、舆论；动词 fari 意为说。

items.en: Old French fame and the learned form renommee carried the sense of public repute.
items.cn: 古法语 fame 及其雅化形式传递「公众声誉」之义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed fame in the thirteenth century, both as rumor and as renown.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪借入 fame，兼指传闻与声望。

items.en: Modern English narrowed fame to positive renown, leaving rumor to another word.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fame 收窄为正面声望，传闻之义让给了别的词。

items.en: Mass media made fame a currency: celebrities are famous for being famous.
items.cn: 大众传媒使 fame 成为一种通货：名人因有名而有名。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root fam- (speak of); near-meaning words name degrees of being known.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fam-（被谈论）；近义组命名「知名」的不同程度。

entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词：fame 的形容词形式
恶名；同根反义

entries.definition: gas or smoke; an angry mood
entries.definitionCN: 气体；怒气；拼写相近但词源不同
盛名；声望（更书面）

entries.definition: the general opinion of a person
entries.definitionCN: 名誉；可好可坏
名人；现代式名气

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for being talked about.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「被谈论」之词的五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin fama meant what people say: fame lives in other people's mouths.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fama＝人们所说的：fame 活在他人的口中。

normal.en: famous, infamy, and defame all carry the same speaking root.
normal.cn: famous、infamy、defame 都含「说」这一词根。

normal.en: a hall of fame is a room full of people everyone talks about.
normal.cn: hall of fame（名人堂）就是满是众口相传之人的一间屋。

normal.en: fame was once rumor too; English gave the rumor job to another word.
normal.cn: fame 一度也指传闻；英语把传闻的活儿交给了别的词。

normal.en: claim to fame means the thing that makes you known.
normal.cn: claim to fame 指让你成名的那件事。

abstract.en: Fame is a crowd's echo of one person's name.
abstract.cn: 名声是人群对一个人名字的回声。

abstract.en: A reputation is a shadow: it follows you and outgrows you.
abstract.cn: 名誉是影子：跟着你，还长得比你大。

abstract.en: Spoken words build ladders; enough of them and the ladder holds a name above the crowd.
abstract.cn: 话语垒成梯子，垒得够多，名字就被举到人群之上。

examples.en: The scientist sought truth rather than fame.
examples.cn: 这位科学家追求真理而非名声。

examples.en: The dish brought the little restaurant local fame.
examples.cn: 这道菜让小餐馆在本地出了名。

examples.en: His fame spread far beyond his own country.
examples.cn: 他的名声远播本国之外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费姆」——费用名目多，人人谈论你，就是 fame（名声）。

root: 拉丁语 fama（传闻、舆论），来自动词 fari（说）。经古法语 fame 进入中古英语，兼指传闻与声望；现代英语收窄为正面名声。同根词 famous、infamy、defame。

sensesIntro.en: From being spoken of outward to good repute and lasting renown.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被谈论」扩展到良好声誉与持久盛名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name traveling from mouth to mouth across a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字在人群中口口相传。

branches.en: THE KNOWING: the state of many mouths.
branches.cn: 知名：众口相传的状态。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: the good half of what is said.
branches.cn: 赞誉：所言之中好的那一半。

branches.en: THE LASTING: renown that survives its season.
branches.cn: 持久：超越一时的盛名。

branches.en: THE CURRENCY: fame as media capital.
branches.cn: 通货：名声作为媒体资本。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: reputation that follows and outgrows its owner.
branches.cn: 影子：跟随主人并比主人更长久的名誉。

intro.en: Fame carries the Latin speaking root fam- through a family of names and reputations.
intro.cn: fame 携拉丁「说」之词根 fam- 构成一族名字与声誉之词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fama and fari seed the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fama 与 fari 孕育整个词族。

items.example: the article led to a defamation suit
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章招致诽谤诉讼

definition_zh: 家庭；家人；（生物分类的）科；语系；家族；一族
definition_en: a group of relatives living together or traced to a common ancestor, or a rank in classification grouping related genera
core_image: 旧相册里，三代人围坐在一张长桌旁，每年夏天在同一个屋檐下合影
scene: 旧相册里，三代人围坐在一张长桌旁，那是这个家庭每年夏天固定的合影。 In the old album the whole family sits around one long table, three generations photographed every summer under the same roof.
sceneCN: 这里 family 是「家庭；家人」（第 1 个义项：共同生活的亲属群体）；句意：旧相册里，三代人围坐在一张长桌旁，那是这个家庭每年夏天固定的合影。

pos.zh: 家庭；家人；科（生物分类）；语系；家族；一族

derivatives.zh: 家庭的；家族性的
熟悉的；亲近的
熟悉；亲近
家族主义（以家族利益为先的社会取向）
家庭归属感（较少用）

senses.title: A household of relatives
senses.definition: a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption, especially parents and their children
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘、婚姻或收养而相关联的一群人，尤指父母与子女
senses.example: The whole family gathers at the same table every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人每年夏天都聚在同一张桌旁。
senses.why: Latin familia first named the household including servants, not only blood kin; English narrowed it toward the kin group while keeping the sense of a shared home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 familia 最初指包括仆役在内的家户，而不只是血亲；英语把它收窄到亲属群体，同时保留「共同居所」的意思。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank family
senses.definition: the rank below order and above genus, grouping genera that share a common ancestry and structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于目之下、属之上的阶元，把共享祖先与结构的若干属聚合在一起
senses.example: The cat family contains several genera and many species.
senses.exampleCN: 猫科包含若干属与许多物种。
senses.why: Taxonomy borrowed a word for a household because a family of organisms is exactly that: several genera living under one name, traced to one ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 分类学借用了「家庭」这个词，因为一个生物科正是如此：若干属在一个名称下，追溯到同一血统。

senses.title: Family-name suffixes in taxonomy
senses.definition: the conventional endings that mark a family, chiefly -aceae for plants and -idae for animals, built on a type genus
senses.definitionCN: 标记科的惯用词尾，植物主要用 -aceae、动物主要用 -idae，均由模式属构成
senses.example: The ending marks the rank before the reader knows the group.
senses.exampleCN: 读者还未知道类群，词尾就已标出这是科。
senses.why: Codes fix the endings so that rank is visible in the word itself; this is why the same root can appear with -aceae in botany and -idae in zoology.
senses.whyCN: 法规固定词尾，使阶元在词形上就能看出；正因此，同一词根在植物学中作 -aceae，在动物学中作 -idae。

senses.title: A language family
senses.definition: a group of languages descended from one reconstructed ancestor, such as the Indo-European family
senses.definitionCN: 从一个重构祖语分化而来的一组语言，如印欧语系
senses.example: The family tree of the languages was drawn before the genetics was known.
senses.exampleCN: 语言的谱系树在遗传学出现之前就已画出。
senses.why: Linguists used the household image for the same reason biologists did: several daughter languages under one reconstructed parent.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家使用家庭意象的理由与生物学家相同：若干派生语言同属一个重构出的母语。

senses.title: A lineage of notable people
senses.definition: a line of related people, often one that has produced several notable figures over generations
senses.definitionCN: 由亲属连成的一条线，常指几代人中出了若干名人的家族
senses.example: A family of printers kept the type in use for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 一个印刷世家让这套字体沿用了两个世纪。
senses.why: The sense is dynastic: the household image extends to inherited craft, name and property rather than to co-residence.
senses.whyCN: 这一义带世家色彩：家庭意象延伸到承袭的手艺、姓氏与财产，而不指共同居住。

senses.title: Nuclear and extended family
senses.definition: the sociological distinction between parents and children alone and a wider kin network including grandparents, aunts and cousins
senses.definitionCN: 社会学上对仅含父母子女与含祖父母、姑舅、表亲等更广亲属网络这两种家庭的区别
senses.example: The survey compared nuclear and extended family households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了核心家庭与扩展家庭住户。
senses.why: Once the word became an object of study, social science needed to specify its shape, and the pair nuclear/extended did that work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词成为研究对象，社会科学需要明确它的形态，核心／扩展这一对词便承担了这项工作。

senses.title: A family of mathematical objects
senses.definition: a collection of sets, curves or functions indexed by a parameter and treated as one object of study
senses.definitionCN: 由参数索引、被当作一个对象研究的一组集合、曲线或函数
senses.example: A family of curves fills the plane as the parameter varies.
senses.exampleCN: 随着参数变化，一族曲线铺满平面。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the household word for a collection whose members are related by a common definition rather than by blood.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个家庭词，指成员由共同定义而非血缘联系起来的一个集合。

senses.title: A product or brand family
senses.definition: a set of related products or models marketed under one name and sharing design or platform
senses.definitionCN: 在同一名称下销售、共享设计或平台的一组相关产品或型号
senses.example: The new model joins the same family as the older sedan.
senses.exampleCN: 新车型与旧款轿车属于同一产品系列。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for the same comfort it gives biology: one name covering several related members, so buyers can predict what they will get.
senses.whyCN: 商业使用这个词，图的是它在生物学中同样的便利：一个名称覆盖若干相关成员，买家因此能预期自己会得到什么。

senses.title: Family as a euphemism or a social unit
senses.titleCN: 作为委婉语或社会单位的「家庭」
senses.definition: an extended use for any close group treated as kin, including chosen families and institutional households
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何被当作亲属看待的紧密群体，包括自主组成的家庭与机构式家庭
senses.example: The residents call the house their family, and the word is not ironic.
senses.exampleCN: 住户们把这所房子称作他们的家庭，这话并不带讽刺。
senses.why: Because the word carries warmth as well as structure, it can be extended to groups that share care rather than descent; the extension is social, not taxonomic.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词既含结构也含温度，它可以延伸到以照料而非血统相联的群体；这一延伸是社会性的，不是分类学的。

intro.en: Family comes from Latin familia 'household', which included servants as well as kin. The word entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate, and the deeper origin of famulus is unsettled.
intro.cn: family 来自拉丁 familia「家户」，其中既有亲属也有仆役。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数，famulus 的更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Familia named the whole household, including slaves and dependants, not only blood relatives; the kin sense was present but not exclusive.
items.cn: familia 指整个家户，包括奴隶与依附者，而不只是血亲；亲属义已存在，但并不独占。

items.en: The household word rests on famulus 'servant'. Its deeper origin is not established; a link to Oscan has been suggested but not demonstrated.
items.cn: 这个家户词基于 famulus「仆役」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出与奥斯坎语有关，但未获证实。

items.en: Old French famille carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where it narrowed toward the kin group.
items.cn: 古法语 famille 在 14 世纪把该词带入英语，词义在那里收窄到亲属群体。

items.en: Linnaeus placed familia in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, and the botanical and zoological codes later fixed its endings.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把 familia 放进他的层级；植物学与动物学法规后来固定了它的词尾。

items.en: Nineteenth-century sociology made the family an object of study and added the nuclear/extended distinction.
items.cn: 19 世纪社会学把家庭变成研究对象，并加入核心／扩展的区分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the descent of familia from famulus is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of famulus is unsettled, so any Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：familia 出自 famulus 这一点一般认为是成立的，但 famulus 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates words that look like family; group two compares the household and the ranks around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形像 family 的词；第二组比较家庭本身与它周围的阶元。

entries.definition: Well known or close, from Latin familiaris 'of a household'. It is the adjective of family, not a second noun.
entries.definitionCN: 熟悉或亲近的，来自拉丁 familiaris「家户的」。它是 family 的形容词，不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: Relating to family, used especially in medicine and genetics, as in familial traits. It is more technical than familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 与家庭或家族有关的，尤用于医学与遗传学，如家族性性状。比 familiar 更技术化。

entries.definition: A severe shortage of food, from Latin fames 'hunger'. It looks like family but has no household in it.
entries.definitionCN: 严重的食物短缺，来自拉丁 fames「饥饿」。外形像 family，却与家户无关。

entries.definition: A social pattern that puts family interests above individual ones. It is built on family with -ism, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 把家族利益置于个人之上的社会模式。由 family 加 -ism 构成，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: All the people living in one house, related or not; it is the older sense of familia without the kin emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 同住一屋的全部人，无论是否亲属；它是 familia 的旧义，但不强调血亲。

entries.definition: Relatives by blood or marriage, seen as a network rather than a household; family overlaps with it but also covers co-residence.
entries.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻相连的亲属，被看作网络而非家户；family 与它重叠，但也包含共同居住。

entries.definition: A line of descent traced through generations. It stresses ancestry, while family can also mean the people alive now.
entries.definitionCN: 按世代追溯的血统线。它强调祖先，而 family 也可指眼下活着的人。

entries.definition: In taxonomy, the rank above family; a family is one step narrower than an order.
entries.definitionCN: 分类学中科之上的阶元；科比目窄一级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: familia was a household, famulus a servant: family began as the people under one roof.
normal.cn: familia 是家户，famulus 是仆役：family 最初就是同一屋顶下的人。

normal.en: The taxonomic family sits between order and genus and is named after a type genus.
normal.cn: 生物学的科位于目与属之间，并以模式属命名。

normal.en: Plant families end in -aceae, animal families in -idae; the ending announces the rank.
normal.cn: 植物科以 -aceae 结尾，动物科以 -idae 结尾；词尾直接宣告阶元。

normal.en: A language family and a family of curves use the same household image: related members under one parent.
normal.cn: 语系与曲线族使用同一个家庭意象：相关成员同属一个父项。

normal.en: Familiar and familial are the two adjectives; famine is a false friend from fames 'hunger'.
normal.cn: familiar 与 familial 是两个形容词；famine 则是来自 fames「饥饿」的假朋友。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where the seating chart has been the same for fifty years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，座次五十年来从未改变。

abstract.en: Picture a surname that arrives before its bearer into every room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个姓氏先于其主人进入每一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of machines sharing one chassis and one nameplate.
abstract.cn: 想象一排机器共用同一个底盘与同一块铭牌。

examples.en: The family has met at the same table every summer for three generations.
examples.cn: 这个家庭三代人每年夏天都在同一张桌旁相聚。

examples.en: The plant family is named after its largest genus.
examples.cn: 这个植物科以它最大的属命名。

examples.en: Two branches of the language family separated before writing existed.
examples.cn: 这个语系的两支在有文字之前就已分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「family 家庭」——同一屋檐下的一群人，后来也指同一祖先下的一群生物 → family 家庭；科

root: 拉丁 familia「家户」，基于 famulus「仆役」，famulus 更深来源不确定；经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of family extend one household image outward: kin at one table, the taxonomic rank, its fixed endings, a language family, a dynasty, nuclear and extended forms, mathematical families, product lines and chosen families.
sensesIntro.cn: family 的九个义项把同一个家户意象向外延伸：同桌的亲人、生物阶元、固定词尾、语系、世家、核心与扩展家庭、数学族、产品系列，以及自主组成的家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one roof over several related members, all answering to one name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片屋顶罩着若干相关成员，全都在一个名称之下。

branches.en: THE HUMAN HOUSEHOLD: blood kin and chosen families that share care rather than descent.
branches.cn: 人的家户：血亲与以照料而非血统相联的自主家庭。

branches.en: THE TAXONOMIC RANK: a family groups genera and announces itself through -aceae or -idae.
branches.cn: 生物阶元：科聚合若干属，并以 -aceae 或 -idae 自我宣告。

branches.en: DESCENT IN LANGUAGE AND CRAFT: daughter languages and dynasties both use the household tree.
branches.cn: 语言与手艺中的传承：派生语言与世家都使用家户树。

branches.en: THE MEASURABLE FORM: nuclear and extended family give the household a shape that surveys can count.
branches.cn: 可测量的形态：核心与扩展家庭给家户一个调查可以计数的形状。

branches.en: ABSTRACT AND COMMERCIAL SETS: mathematical families and product families share a definition rather than blood.
branches.cn: 抽象与商业集合：数学族与产品族共享定义而非血缘。

intro.en: Family is a household word that spread into taxonomy, linguistics and mathematics without losing its shape: several related members under one name.
intro.cn: family 是一个家户词，扩散到分类学、语言学与数学，却没有失去原有形状：若干相关成员在一个名称之下。

latinIntro.en: Latin familia gives family, familiar, familial and familism; famulus gives the household core, and famine is unrelated, from fames 'hunger'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 familia 给出 family、familiar、familial、familism；famulus 提供家户核心；famine 无关，出自 fames「饥饿」。

items.example: Familia included dependants as well as kin.
items.exampleCN: familia 既含亲属，也含依附者。

items.example: The household word rests on famulus.
A familiar face belongs to the household circle.
items.exampleCN: 熟悉的面孔属于家户圈子。

items.example: Familial traits run in the pedigree.
items.exampleCN: 家族性性状在谱系中传递。

items.example: Rosaceae is built on the type genus Rosa.
items.exampleCN: 蔷薇科由模式属 Rosa 构成。

items.example: Felidae is built on the type genus Felis.
items.exampleCN: 猫科由模式属 Felis 构成。

items.example: Familism shaped the local marriage rules.
items.exampleCN: 家族主义塑造了当地的婚姻规则。

definition_zh: 著名的；出名的；驰名的；（旧）极好的
definition_en: known by very many people, or celebrated for a particular quality
core_image: 景点门口的铜牌上刻着一行金字，游客举着地图纷纷指向它
scene: 游客们举着导览手册，在古城门前排起长队，导游举旗讲解。The guide pointed to the famous gate built eight hundred years ago.
sceneCN: 这里指「著名的」，对应第 1 个义项：被极多人知晓；句意为导游指向八百年前修建的著名城门。画面要点：导游旗、长队、斑驳的城门。

pos.zh: 著名的；出名的；（旧）极好的

derivatives.zh: 名声（同根名词：被谈论的状态）
声名狼藉的（否定前缀，坏的那半名声）
声名狼藉地（副词化）
有名的（过去分词作形容词，稍书面）
著名地；（口语）非常友好地

senses.title: Known by very many people
senses.definition: known or recognized by very many people
senses.definitionCN: 被极多的人知晓或认得
senses.example: The Great Wall is famous worldwide.
senses.why: To be much spoken of is to be known; the adjective pinned the talk to recognition.
senses.whyCN: 被大量谈论即被知晓；形容词把「谈论」钉在「认得」上。

senses.title: Celebrated for something good
senses.definition: well known and admired for a particular quality or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因某种品质或成就而广受称道
senses.example: The city is famous for its food.
senses.why: The old Latin word was neutral, but English chose the praising half.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语旧词本是中性的，英语选择了赞美的一半。

senses.title: Excellent, in older use
senses.definition: first-rate, excellent, in older or informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 一流的、极好的，用于旧式或口语
senses.example: We had a famous time at the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在集市上玩得极开心。
senses.why: Enough praise slides from 'talked about' to 'the very best'.
senses.whyCN: 赞美累积，便从「被谈论」滑向「最好」。

intro.en: Famous descends from Latin fama, 'what people say', through its adjective form meaning 'much talked of'.
intro.cn: famous 源自拉丁语 fama（人们所说的），经由意为「被大量谈论的」形容词形式传入。

items.en: Latin fama meant report and public opinion; famosus meant much talked of, whether praised or blamed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fama 意为传闻与舆论；famosus 指被大量谈论，可褒可贬。

items.en: Medieval Latin famosus often carried the sense of renowned, honored.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 famosus 常带「有名望、受尊崇」之义。

items.en: Old French fameus passed the word into England with the positive reading.
items.cn: 古法语 fameus 把带正面色彩的词传入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English famous meant celebrated and renowned from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语自十四世纪起即以 famous 表示 celebrated、renowned。

items.en: Modern English fixed famous as purely positive: famous for, world-famous.
items.cn: 现代英语把 famous 固定为纯粹的褒义：famous for、world-famous。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin fam- root or the -ous ending; near-meaning words name degrees and flavors of being known.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fam- 或 -ous 词尾；近义组命名「知名」的不同程度与色彩。

entries.definition: the noun of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词：名声
声名狼藉的；同根反义
极好的；也指难以置信的；词源为 fabula「故事」
有名望的；更书面

entries.definition: known by many, milder than famous
entries.definitionCN: 广为人知的；语气弱于 famous
臭名昭著的；贬义

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the adjective of being talked about.
normalIntro.cn: 「被谈论」的形容词，五个抓手。

normal.en: famous is fame plus -ous: full of being talked about.
normal.cn: famous＝fame+-ous：充满「被谈论」。

normal.en: be famous for names the cause, be famous as names the role.
normal.cn: famous for 接原因，famous as 接身份。

normal.en: notorious is famous gone bad: known for the wrong reasons.
normal.cn: notorious 是变坏的 famous：因错事而知名。

normal.en: world-famous is one hyphen that raises the scale.
normal.cn: world-famous 用一个连字符把规模升到全球。

normal.en: famous last words is a joke phrase for overconfident predictions.
normal.cn: famous last words 是反讽语，嘲笑过度自信的预言。

abstract.en: A famous face is one the crowd has already met before the person arrives.
abstract.cn: 著名的面孔，是人在到达之前人群就已见过的脸。

abstract.en: Recognition is a spotlight that follows some names and hunts others.
abstract.cn: 认可是探照灯，追随某些名字，追逐另一些。

abstract.en: To be known for one thing is to have a door with a name plate on it.
abstract.cn: 因一事而闻名，就是拥有一扇挂着名牌的门。

examples.en: The museum is famous for its ancient coins.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆以古钱币闻名。

examples.en: She became famous almost overnight after the film.
examples.cn: 电影上映后她几乎一夜成名。

examples.en: This tea is famous all over the country.
examples.cn: 这种茶闻名全国。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费默斯」——费用沉默不了，人人都在谈论你 → 著名的。

root: 拉丁语 fama（传闻、舆论）的形容词 famosus（被大量谈论的）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 fameus 进入英语，词义从可褒可贬收窄为正面声望。同根词 fame、infamous、defame。

sensesIntro.en: From being known by many outward to celebrated praise and an older sense of excellence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「广为人知」扩展到因优而名的称颂与旧义的「极好」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name everyone in the crowd already knows.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中人人早已知道的名字。

branches.en: THE RECOGNITION: known by the many.
branches.cn: 认得：被众人知晓。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: known for something good.
branches.cn: 称颂：因好事而知名。

branches.en: THE SUPERLATIVE: excellent, in older speech.
branches.cn: 最高级：旧用法中的极好。

branches.en: THE LANDMARK: places and dishes known for their fame.
branches.cn: 地标：因名声而知名的地方与菜肴。

branches.en: THE PEAK: the praising reading climbing to 'the very best'.
branches.cn: 顶峰：赞美义攀升至「最好」。

intro.en: Famous is the fam- speaking root wearing the -ous suffix; its family is all about talk and repute.
intro.cn: famous 是 fam-（说）词根戴上 -ous 词尾；词族围绕谈论与声誉。

latinIntro.en: Latin fama and famosus seed the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fama 与 famosus 孕育词族。

definition_zh: 扇子；风扇；扇形；爱好者；粉丝；扇（风）
definition_en: a device or shape that moves air, or an enthusiastic supporter; also, to stir air
core_image: 一把折扇缓缓张开成弧，风从扇面掠过看台上一片摇动的荧光棒
scene: 演唱会开场前，观众挥舞着灯牌，有人在入口处领取折扇。Every fan in the stadium waved a glowing paper paddle.
sceneCN: 这里同时出现两个义项：观众是「狂热爱好者」（第 3 个义项），手持之物即「扇子」（第 1 个义项）；句意为体育场里每位粉丝挥舞一把发光的纸扇。画面要点：看台、灯牌、发光折扇。

derivatives.zh: 狂热者；狂热的（fan 的全形词源）
狂热的（fanatic 加形容词后缀）
狂热地（副词化）
粉丝群体（复合名词）
粉丝圈（口语新造词）

senses.title: A device that moves air
senses.definition: an instrument with a surface or blades that stirs the air
senses.definitionCN: 以扇面或叶片搅动空气的器具
senses.example: The ceiling fan turned slowly.
senses.why: The winnowing basket blew the chaff; the tool is defined by moving air.
senses.whyCN: 扬谷之具吹走糠皮；器物以「扇动空气」为定义。

senses.title: To move air toward something
senses.definition: to move or wave something to make a current of air
senses.definitionCN: 挥动某物以产生气流
senses.example: She fanned the fire gently.
senses.why: The noun takes a verb seat and does its own work: air goes where the fan points.
senses.whyCN: 名词登上动词之位，亲自动手：风随扇向。

senses.title: An enthusiastic supporter
senses.definition: an ardent admirer or supporter of a person, team, or art
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、球队或艺术的狂热仰慕者
senses.example: He is a big fan of that band.
senses.exampleCN: 他是那个乐队的铁杆粉丝。
senses.why: The worshipper of temples became the worshipper of stars.
