senses.title: A shape spreading from one point
senses.definition: a shape that spreads out from a narrow point like an open fan
senses.definitionCN: 从一个窄点展开、形似张开的扇子的形状
senses.example: The cards lay out in a fan.
senses.why: The open hand-fan gives its outline to anything that spreads the same way.
senses.whyCN: 张开的手扇把轮廓借给一切同样展开之物。

intro.en: Fan is two words in one spelling: the older noun is Latin vannus, a winnowing basket; the newer one is a shortening of fanatic.
intro.cn: fan 的同一拼写下藏着两个词：旧的是拉丁语 vannus（扬谷的簸箕），新的是 fanatic 的缩略。

items.en: Latin vannus meant a basket for tossing grain in the wind to blow away chaff.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vannus 指在风中扬谷、吹去糠皮的工具。

items.en: Old English fann kept the winnowing-basket sense; the tool later gained a blade.
items.cn: 古英语 fann 保留扬谷具之义；这种工具后来装上了叶片。

items.en: Modern English fan came to mean any device that stirs air, from hand fans to machines.
items.cn: 现代英语 fan 泛指一切扇动空气的器具，从手扇到电扇。

items.en: Latin fanaticus meant inspired by a temple frenzy; frantic worship.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fanaticus 指受神庙狂热驱使的；狂热的崇拜。

items.en: Nineteenth-century American baseball crowds were called fans, a clipping of fanatic.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国棒球观众被称为 fans，即 fanatic 的缩略。

note.en: Look-alikes share spelling; near-meaning words name both the air-moving tool and the devoted follower.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写；近义组同时覆盖「扇风之物」与「狂热追随者」。

entries.definitionCN: 乐趣；仅一字母之差，词源无关

entries.definition: a person filled with excessive zeal
entries.definitionCN: 狂热者；fan 的完整形式
厢式车；与扬谷具 vannus 相差一字母
追随者；语气更平

entries.definition: a person keen on an activity

仰慕者；感情较深

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a word that hides two histories behind one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拼写藏着两段历史的词，五个抓手。

normal.en: The air-moving fan came from Latin vannus, a winnowing basket.
normal.cn: 扇风之 fan 出自拉丁 vannus，簸箕扬谷。

normal.en: The fan who cheers came from fanatic, clipped in baseball stands.
normal.cn: 欢呼的 fan 出自 fanatic，看台上剪短而成。

normal.en: fan the flames means to stir up trouble or feeling.
normal.cn: fan the flames 意为煽风点火。

normal.en: Cards and peacocks spread in a fan shape.
normal.cn: 纸牌与孔雀尾羽都展开成扇形。

normal.en: fun and fan differ by one letter: fans have fun.
normal.cn: fun 与 fan 只差一个字母：粉丝就是来找乐子的。

abstract.en: A fan is wind with a handle; devotion is wind with a face.
abstract.cn: 扇子是有柄的风；热爱是有脸的风。

abstract.en: One narrow point, and everything opens outward: the fan teaches spreading.
abstract.cn: 一个窄点，一切向外展开：扇形教人展开。

abstract.en: Fandom is a stadium-sized heartbeat all beating for one name.
abstract.cn: 粉丝圈是体育场大小的心跳，为同一个名字跳动。

examples.en: Turn on the fan; the room is stuffy.
examples.cn: 把风扇打开，屋里闷。

examples.en: Thousands of fans waited outside the theatre.
examples.cn: 数千名粉丝在剧院外等候。

examples.en: He fanned the papers across the desk.
examples.cn: 他把文件在桌上摊成扇形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「粉」——粉丝手中挥着粉色的折扇，fan 既是粉丝也是扇子。

root: 一词两源：器具义出自拉丁 vannus（簸箕），经古英语 fann 传入；爱好者义是拉丁 fanaticus（狂热的）的十九世纪缩略。两词在现代拼写中合流为 fan。

sensesIntro.en: From air-moving tools outward to the verb, the follower, and the spreading shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 从扇风之器扩展到动词、狂热者与展开之形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air and ardor moving outward from one held point.
core.cn: 核心意象：风与热忱从同一个持握点向外涌动。

branches.en: THE TOOL: anything built to stir air.
branches.cn: 器具：一切为搅动空气而造之物。

branches.en: THE MOTION: waving air into being.
branches.cn: 动作：把风挥动出来。

branches.en: THE FOLLOWER: clipped from fanatic.
branches.cn: 追随者：fanatic 的缩略。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: anything opening like the tool.
branches.cn: 形状：像器具一样展开之物。

branches.en: THE STIRRED-UP CROWD: fans whose feeling is fanned.
branches.cn: 被煽动的人群：热情被扇旺的粉丝。

intro.en: Fan is a short word with a long shadow: fanatic, fandom, and fanbase all grow from the clipping.
intro.cn: fan 是个短词却拖着长影：fanatic、fandom、fanbase 都从缩略形长出。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives both roots: vannus for the tool, fanaticus for the follower.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出两个词根：vannus 是工具，fanaticus 是追随者。

items.example: the singer has a loyal fan base
items.exampleCN: 歌手拥有忠实的粉丝群

definition_zh: 极好的；了不起的；幻想的；奇异的；（数量）大得惊人的
definition_en: extraordinarily good, imaginary, bizarre, or impossibly large
core_image: 烟花在夜空炸开成不存在的花，围观的人齐声喊出同一个赞叹词
scene: 科学展上机器人完成了高难动作，全班同学一起欢呼鼓掌。The robot's dance was fantastic, and the whole class cheered.
sceneCN: 这里指「极好的」，对应第 1 个义项：好得超出寻常；句意为机器人的舞蹈太精彩了，全班都欢呼。画面要点：机器人、展台、鼓掌的同学们。

pos.zh: 极好的；幻想的；奇异的；大得惊人的

幻想（旧式拼法，现罕用）

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: extraordinarily good or attractive
senses.definitionCN: 特别好或特别吸引人
senses.example: The party was fantastic.
senses.why: Daily speech borrowed the exaggeration of imagination as praise.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语借来想象的夸张当赞美。

senses.title: Imaginary or unreal
senses.definition: based on imagination rather than reality
senses.definitionCN: 基于想象而非现实
senses.example: The novel is set in a fantastic kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说设定在一个幻想王国。
senses.why: The original Greek sense: what appears only in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原义：只在心中显现之物。

senses.title: Strangely shaped or extravagant
senses.definition: strange, extravagant, or bizarre in form
senses.definitionCN: 外形奇异、铺张或怪诞
senses.example: Fantastic towers crowned the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 怪异的塔楼耸立在宫殿上。
senses.why: What imagination builds often looks strange to plain eyes.
senses.whyCN: 想象所造之物，在朴素眼光里往往显得怪异。

senses.title: Impossibly large in amount
senses.definition: so large that it seems unreal
senses.definitionCN: 大到仿佛不真实
senses.example: He was offered a fantastic sum.
senses.exampleCN: 有人给他一笔大得惊人的款项。
senses.why: Numbers beyond belief are numbers from a fantasy.
senses.whyCN: 大到难以置信的数字，是从幻想里来的数字。

intro.en: Fantastic goes back to Greek phantastikos, 'able to present to the mind', from phainesthai, 'to appear'.
intro.cn: fantastic 回溯希腊语 phantastikos（能在心中呈现的），出自 phainesthai（显现）。

items.en: Greek phantastikos described images that appear in the mind; phantasia meant appearance or imagination.
items.cn: 希腊语 phantastikos 描述心中显现的影像；phantasia 意为显现或想象。

items.en: Latin phantasticus borrowed the word for imaginary, spectral things.
items.cn: 拉丁语 phantasticus 借入该词，指想象中的、如幻影般的事物。

items.en: Old French fantastique carried the word toward England.
items.cn: 古法语 fantastique 把该词送往英格兰。

items.en: Middle English fantastic meant existing only in imagination, often with a hint of absurdity.
items.cn: 中古英语 fantastic 意为只存在于想象之中，常带荒诞意味。

items.en: Modern English split the word: imaginative in art criticism, 'excellent' in everyday speech.
items.cn: 现代英语让该词分岔：艺术批评中指「富于想象」，日常口语指「极好」。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root phant- (what appears); near-meaning words name degrees of excellence and imagination.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 phant-（显现之物）；近义组命名「极好」的程度与想象之域。

entries.definitionCN: 同根名词：幻想、想象世界

entries.definition: a ghost, an appearance without substance

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a Greek word for what appears in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 希腊语「心中显现之物」，五个抓手。

normal.en: fantastic and fantasy share the Greek root for what appears in the mind.
normal.cn: fantastic 与 fantasy 共享希腊语「心中显现」的词根。

normal.en: Everyday speech uses fantastic as the strongest everyday praise: fantastic idea, fantastic view.
normal.cn: 日常口语把 fantastic 当最强的称赞：fantastic idea、fantastic view。

normal.en: phantom keeps the ph- spelling of the same Greek root.
normal.cn: phantom 保留同一希腊词根的 ph- 拼法。

normal.en: Fantastic Beasts put the old 'imaginary' sense in a title.
normal.cn: 《神奇动物》（Fantastic Beasts）把旧的「想象」义放进了片名。

normal.en: a fantastic sum means an amount too big to seem real.
normal.cn: a fantastic sum 指大到不像真实存在的金额。

abstract.en: Imagination is a projector; fantastic is the light it throws.
abstract.cn: 想象是放映机；fantastic 是它投出的光。

abstract.en: Praise is exaggeration domesticated: fantastic tames wonder into a compliment.
abstract.cn: 赞美是被驯化的夸张：fantastic 把惊叹驯成一句恭维。

abstract.en: What appears only in the mind casts the longest shadow on paper.
abstract.cn: 只在心中显现之物，在纸上投下最长的影子。

examples.en: You did a fantastic job on the project.
examples.cn: 你在这个项目上做得太出色了。

examples.en: The story takes place in a fantastic world of talking animals.
examples.cn: 故事发生在一个动物会说话的幻想世界。

examples.en: They paid a fantastic price for the small flat.
examples.cn: 他们为这套小公寓付了高得离谱的价钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「范太斯提克」——范老师夸得太厉害（太斯提克），就是 fantastic（极好的）。

root: 希腊语 phantastikos（心中可呈现的），出自 phainesthai（显现）；经拉丁语 phantasticus 与古法语 fantastique 进入英语。词义从「想象的、荒诞的」分岔出「极好的」口语义。

sensesIntro.en: From mind-born images outward to praise, strangeness, and impossible size.
sensesIntro.cn: 从心中所生影像扩展到赞美、怪异与大得离谱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light thrown by the mind's projector onto the world.
core.cn: 核心意象：心灵的放映机投向世界的光。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: the everyday excellent.
branches.cn: 赞美：日常的「极好」。

branches.en: THE IMAGINARY: the original Greek sense.
branches.cn: 想象：希腊语原义。

branches.en: THE BIZARRE: what imagination builds looks strange.
branches.cn: 怪诞：想象之物显得奇异。

branches.en: THE IMMENSE: amounts that seem unreal.
branches.cn: 巨大：仿佛不真实的数量。

branches.en: THE BRIDGE: praise borrows the exaggeration of fantasy.
branches.cn: 桥梁：赞美借用幻想的夸张。

intro.en: Fantastic is the Greek appearing-root in an adjective suit; the family includes fantasy, phantom, and fancy's neighbours.
intro.cn: fantastic 是希腊「显现」词根穿上形容词外衣；词族包含 fantasy、phantom 等。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia traveled through Latin phantasticus into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 phantasia 经拉丁 phantasticus 进入英语。

definition_en: at, to, or from a great distance, or to a great degree

scene: 站台上望着远去的列车，同学挥手直到看不见为止。The train rolled away and grew small, going far down the line.

senses.title: At or to a great distance
senses.definition: at, to, or from a great distance
senses.definitionCN: 在很远的地方，或达到很远的距离
senses.example: The station is not far from here.
senses.why: Distance is the root meaning; everything else measures along it.
senses.whyCN: 距离是词根义；其余义项都沿它度量。

senses.title: Much or to a great extent
senses.definition: very much, or to a great degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 非常，或达到很大程度
senses.example: The result is far better than expected.
senses.why: Long distance becomes long degree: far maps space onto amount.
senses.whyCN: 长距离变成长程度：far 把空间映射到数量。

senses.title: Distant in time or remote in relation
senses.definition: remote in time, or distant in similarity or connection
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上久远，或在相似与联系上疏远
senses.example: The far past is hard to imagine.
senses.why: Space stretches into time and into how closely things are tied.
senses.whyCN: 空间延伸为时间，也延伸为事物联系的紧密程度。

senses.title: The far side or end
senses.definition: more distant of two, as in the far side or far end
senses.definitionCN: 两者中较远的，如 far side、far end
senses.example: He sat at the far end of the table.
senses.why: Among two distances, far picks the longer one.
senses.whyCN: 在两个距离之间，far 挑出更长的那个。

intro.en: Far is a native English adverb and adjective, straight from Old English feorr, with Germanic cousins everywhere.
intro.cn: far 是英语本族的副词兼形容词，直接出自古英语 feorr，在日耳曼诸语中亲戚遍地。

items.en: The reconstructed root ferhaz meant far, distant; the same root gives German fern.
items.cn: 重构词根 ferhaz 意为远的；德语 fern 同根。

items.en: Old English feorr served as both adjective and adverb: a feorr land, to travel feorr.
items.cn: 古英语 feorr 兼作形容词与副词：远方的土地、远行。

items.en: Middle English far and ferre kept both uses; comparatives ferther, farther grew from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 far、ferre 保留两种用法，并长出 farther、further。

items.en: Early Modern English fixed far as the positive of farther and further.
items.cn: 早期现代英语把 far 定为 farther、further 的原级。

items.en: Modern English spread far into phrases: far away, so far, far from it.
items.cn: 现代英语让 far 走进无数短语：far away、so far、far from it。

note.en: Look-alikes share the single syllable; near-meaning words name distances and degrees of remoteness.
note.cn: 形近组共享单音节外形；近义组命名距离与疏远的程度。

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the shortest distance word.
normalIntro.cn: 最短的「距离」词，五个抓手。

normal.en: far has two comparatives: farther for distance, further for degree.
normal.cn: far 有两个比较级：farther 指距离，further 指程度。

normal.en: so far means up to now: the best results so far.
normal.cn: so far 意为「到目前为止」。

normal.en: by far picks the clear winner: the best by far.
normal.cn: by far 表示「远远地」：遥遥领先。

normal.en: far from it means the opposite is true.
normal.cn: far from it 表示「恰恰相反」。

normal.en: German fern is a cousin of far.
normal.cn: 德语 fern 与 far 同源。

abstract.en: Distance is the mind's ruler; far is where the ruler runs out.
abstract.cn: 距离是心里的尺子；far 是尺子刻度穷尽之处。

abstract.en: Some goals are far, not in kilometers but in years.
abstract.cn: 有些目标之远，不在公里，而在年月。

abstract.en: The far past is a country with no roads left.
abstract.cn: 遥远的过去是一个没有路可通的国度。

examples.en: The hospital is far from the village.
examples.cn: 医院离村子很远。

examples.en: This is by far the best answer.
examples.cn: 这显然是最好的答案。

examples.en: The plan is far from perfect.
examples.cn: 这个计划远非完美。

sensesIntro.en: From spatial distance outward to degree, time, relation, and the far end of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从空间距离扩展到程度、时间、关系与事物的远端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road that keeps going after your eyes give up.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛看不清之后仍在延伸的路。

branches.en: THE DISTANCE: the root spatial sense.
branches.cn: 距离：词根的空间义。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: much, as measured on the distance ruler.
branches.cn: 程度：用距离尺子度量的「多」。

branches.en: THE REMOTE: distant times and loose ties.
branches.cn: 疏远：久远的时间与松散的联系。

branches.en: THE FAR END: the more distant of two.
branches.cn: 远端：两者中较远者。

branches.en: THE RULER: one scale for both space and amount.
branches.cn: 尺子：空间与数量共用同一刻度。

intro.en: Far is a bare Germanic root; its family grows through comparatives and compounds.
intro.cn: far 是裸的日耳曼词根；词族靠比较级与复合词生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no member of this Germanic family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这个日耳曼词族中没有成员。

senses.title: A place where crops or animals are raised
senses.definition: an area of land with buildings used for growing crops or raising animals
senses.definitionCN: 种植作物或饲养牲畜的土地与建筑
senses.example: They run a dairy farm.
senses.why: The leased land became the working land; the place swallowed the lease.
senses.whyCN: 租来的土地变成了劳作的土地；场所吞没了租约。

senses.title: The business of agriculture
senses.definition: the activity of growing crops or raising animals as a business
senses.definitionCN: 以种植或养殖为业的经营活动
senses.example: Farming is hard work.
senses.why: The place name became the name of the trade done there.
senses.whyCN: 地名变成了在那里所从事之业的名字。

senses.title: To grow crops or raise animals
senses.definition: to use land for growing crops or keeping animals
senses.definitionCN: 用土地种植作物或饲养动物
senses.example: The family has farmed this valley for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人在这条山谷耕种了几代。
senses.why: Once the land is yours to work, working it becomes a verb.
senses.whyCN: 土地既可劳作，劳作便成动词。

senses.title: A place producing one thing in quantity
senses.definition: any site that produces large amounts of one thing
senses.definitionCN: 大量产出单一产品的地方
senses.example: A wind farm covers the hillside.
senses.why: The farm pattern of single large output copied itself onto energy and data.
senses.whyCN: 农场式的大批量单一产出，复制到了能源与数据领域。

intro.en: Farm goes back to Latin firma, 'a fixed payment', a lease; the working of leased land gave the modern meaning.
intro.cn: farm 回溯拉丁语 firma「固定的款项」，即租约；在租来的土地上劳作产生了现代意义。

items.en: Latin firmare meant to fix or settle; firma was a fixed annual payment.
items.cn: 拉丁语 firmare 意为固定、议定；firma 指固定的年款。

items.en: Medieval Latin firma named the rent paid for land held from a lord.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 firma 指向领主承租土地所付的地租。

items.en: Old French ferme carried the lease and its fixed payment into England.
items.cn: 古法语 ferme 把租约及其固定款项带入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English farm first meant the rent itself, then the leased land.
items.cn: 中古英语 farm 先指租金本身，后指租种的土地。

items.en: Modern English extended farm to the whole agricultural holding: buildings, animals, and work.
items.cn: 现代英语把 farm 扩展为整个农事单位：建筑、牲畜与劳作。

note.en: Look-alikes share the firm stem; near-meaning words name places and ways of growing food.
note.cn: 形近组共享 firm 词干外形；近义组命名生产食物的场所与方式。

entries.definition: a large farm for animals, especially in America
entries.definitionCN: 大牧场（尤指美洲）

entries.definition: a large farm for one crop
entries.definitionCN: 种植园；单一作物的大农场

entries.definition: the science and practice of farming
entries.definitionCN: 农业；农耕的总称

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for a fixed payment that became the land itself.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「固定款项」如何变成土地本身，五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin firma meant a fixed payment: farm began as rent, not soil.
normal.cn: 拉丁 firma＝固定款项：farm 起点是租金，不是土壤。

normal.en: farm, farmer, farming: the place grows a person and a trade.
normal.cn: farm、farmer、farming：场所长出人与职业。

normal.en: wind farm and solar farm borrow the farm pattern for energy.
normal.cn: wind farm、solar farm 把农场模式借给能源。

normal.en: firm, the Latin cousin, still means both solid and a company.
normal.cn: 拉丁表亲 firm 至今兼指「结实的」与「公司」。

normal.en: farmhouse, farmland, farmyard are compounds built on farm.
normal.cn: farmhouse、farmland、farmyard 都是以 farm 构成的复合词。

abstract.en: A farm is a contract written into the soil: fixed work, fixed seasons.
abstract.cn: 农场是写进土壤的契约：固定的劳作，固定的季节。

abstract.en: Furrows are the farm's lined paper, one row a sentence.
abstract.cn: 田垄是农场的稿纸，一垄一句话。

abstract.en: Every harvest is rent paid to the land itself.
abstract.cn: 每一次收成，都是付给土地本身的租金。

examples.en: Grandpa has farmed the same field for forty years.
examples.cn: 爷爷在同一块田里耕作了四十年。

examples.en: The farm sells fresh eggs at the market every Saturday.
examples.cn: 这家农场每周六在集市卖鲜鸡蛋。

examples.en: Fish farming has grown quickly along the coast.
examples.cn: 沿海的水产养殖发展很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法姆」——法（租约）+ 姆（亩）：按亩付租的法子，就是 farm（农场）。

root: 拉丁语 firma（固定款项、地租），来自 firmare（议定、固定），与 firmus（结实的）同根。经古法语 ferme 进入中古英语，先指租金，后指租地，最终扩展为整个农业生产单位。

sensesIntro.en: From a fixed lease outward to the land, the trade, the verb, and mass production.
sensesIntro.cn: 从固定租约扩展到土地、行业、动词与批量产出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soil under contract — work fixed by seasons and payment.
core.cn: 核心意象：契约下的土壤——劳作被季节与支付固定。

branches.en: THE PLACE: land and buildings of agriculture.
branches.cn: 场所：农业的土地与建筑。

branches.en: THE TRADE: agriculture as a business.
branches.cn: 行业：作为生意的农业。

branches.en: THE ACTION: to grow and raise.
branches.cn: 动作：种植与养殖。

branches.en: THE COPY: farms of wind, sun, and fish.
branches.cn: 复制：风电场、太阳能电站与养殖场。

branches.en: THE LEASE ROOTED: payment turned into ploughed soil.
branches.cn: 租约扎根：支付化为犁过的土壤。

intro.en: Farm carries the Latin firm- (fix, settle) root beside firm and affirm.
intro.cn: farm 携拉丁 firm-（固定、议定）词根，与 firm、affirm 比邻。

latinIntro.en: Latin firmus, firma, and firmare seed the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 firmus、firma、firmare 孕育词族。

items.meaning: the enclosed area of a farm

items.example: a firm handshake; a law firm
items.exampleCN: 有力的握手；律师事务所

definition_en: a person who owns, manages, or works on a farm
core_image: 草帽下晒黑的脸，晨光里拖拉机后扬起的尘土与翻开的田垄
scene: 收获节上，学生把新摘的玉米送到集市，摊位主人正是在地头耕作的老人。The farmer who grew the corn waved at the students.
sceneCN: 这里指「农民」，对应第 1 个义项：经营或耕作农场之人；句意为种出玉米的农民向学生们挥手。画面要点：集市摊位、成筐玉米、草帽。

senses.title: A person who owns or works a farm
senses.definition: a person who owns, manages, or works on a farm
senses.definitionCN: 拥有、经营农场或在农场劳作的人
senses.example: The farmer rises before the sun.
senses.why: The -er suffix puts a person where the farm was: the land's worker gets the land's name.
senses.whyCN: -er 词尾把人安放进农场之位：劳作者获得土地之名。

senses.title: A person who pays to work leased land
senses.definition: one who cultivates land belonging to another for a share or rent
senses.definitionCN: 为分成或租金而为他人耕作土地之人
senses.example: The tenant farmer pays rent each spring.
senses.why: The oldest sense: the leaseholder of the firma, still alive in tenant farmer.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项：firma 的承租人，仍活在 tenant farmer 之中。

senses.title: One who cultivates something metaphorically
senses.definition: one who raises or cultivates something as a business
senses.definitionCN: 以培育或经营某物为业者
senses.example: A pearl farmer tends the oyster beds.
senses.exampleCN: 珍珠养殖者照料牡蛎场。
senses.why: Wherever careful raising happens, farm grows a farmer.
senses.whyCN: 凡有精心培育之处，farm 都会长出 farmer。

intro.en: Farmer is simply farm plus the agent suffix -er: the person who holds and works the land, from the lease word firma.
intro.cn: farmer 就是 farm 加施动者词尾 -er：持有并耕作土地之人，词源是租约词 firma。

items.en: Latin firma was the fixed payment for land; firmare meant to settle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 firma 是土地的固定款项；firmare 意为议定。

items.en: Old French ferme named both the lease and the leased land.
items.cn: 古法语 ferme 兼指租约与租来的土地。

items.en: Middle English farm meant rent, then land; fermour named the one who paid it and tilled it.
items.cn: 中古英语 farm 先指租金后指土地；fermour 指付租并耕作之人。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the farmer came to mean the occupier who works the farm himself.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，farmer 专指亲自经营农场之人。

items.en: Modern English farmer covers owners and tenants alike, the backbone word of agriculture.
items.cn: 现代英语 farmer 兼指农场主与佃农，是农业的核心称谓。

note.en: Look-alikes share the farm stem or the -er agent suffix; near-meaning words name workers of the land.
note.cn: 形近组共享 farm 词干或 -er 施动者词尾；近义组命名在土地上劳作的人。

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the person the land named.
normalIntro.cn: 被土地命名的人，五个抓手。

normal.en: farmer is farm plus -er: the person at the farm.
normal.cn: farmer＝farm+-er：在农场的那个人。

normal.en: The root firm- means fixed: farm was first a fixed rent, so the farmer was first the rent-payer.
normal.cn: 词根 firm-＝固定：farm 最初是固定租金，farmer 最初是交租者。

normal.en: tenant farmer keeps the old lease sense alive.
normal.cn: tenant farmer 保留了古老的租地义。

normal.en: farmer's market sells food straight from its growers.
normal.cn: farmer's market 把农产品从种植者手里直卖给你。

normal.en: Peasant and farmer differ in tone: farmer is the neutral word.
normal.cn: peasant 与 farmer 语域不同：farmer 是中性词。

abstract.en: A farmer is a person who argues with weather and wins some years.
abstract.cn: 农民是与天气谈判的人，有些年头能赢。

abstract.en: To farm is to sign a yearly contract with the soil.
abstract.cn: 务农是每年与土壤签一次约。

abstract.en: The -er suffix turns places into people; the farm stands up and puts on a hat.
abstract.cn: -er 把场所变成人；农场站起来，戴上了草帽。

examples.en: The farmer repaired the fence before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 农民赶在暴风雨前修好了栅栏。

examples.en: Farmers brought their best vegetables to the market.
examples.cn: 农民们把最好的蔬菜带到市场。

examples.en: Her uncle is a farmer in the northern plains.
examples.cn: 她叔叔是北部平原上的农民。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法姆」加「儿」——法（租）母（亩）之儿，种地的人就是 farmer。

root: farm（拉丁 firma「固定款项」经古法语 ferme）加施动者后缀 -er。词义从「付租耕作者」演变为「农场经营者」，是 farm 词族中的核心人称词。

sensesIntro.en: From the land's worker outward to the leaseholder and the cultivator of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从土地的劳作者扩展到租地人与比喻中的培育者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing where the lease met the soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在租约与土壤交汇处的人。

branches.en: THE WORKER: the person of the farm.
branches.cn: 劳作者：农场的人。

branches.en: THE TENANT: the oldest lease sense.
branches.cn: 佃农：最古老的租地义。

branches.en: THE CULTIVATOR: raising things beyond crops.
branches.cn: 培育者：作物之外的养殖者。

branches.en: THE ROOT: firma the fixed payment beneath the person.
branches.cn: 词根：人之下是固定款项 firma。

branches.en: THE FEEDER: the farmer who feeds the town.
branches.cn: 供养者：喂养城镇的农民。

intro.en: Farmer is the cleanest -er word in the farm family; the suffix turns the place into a person.
intro.cn: farmer 是 farm 词族中最干净的 -er 词；词尾把场所变成人。

latinIntro.en: Latin firma and firmare lie beneath the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 firma 与 firmare 支撑整个词族。

definition_zh: 使着迷；迷住；使心醉神迷
definition_en: to hold someone's attention completely, as if under a spell
core_image: 篝火在黑暗中跳动，围观者的眼睛映着火光，谁也挪不动脚步
scene: 自然课上老师放了一段深海录像，发光的水母缓缓漂过屏幕。The glowing jellyfish fascinated the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里指「使着迷」，对应第 1 个义项：强烈吸引使其无法移开目光；句意为发光的水母把全班迷住了。画面要点：暗教室、屏幕蓝光、发光水母。

pos.zh: 使着迷；迷住；使神魂颠倒

derivatives.zh: 迷人的（现在分词作形容词）
着迷的（过去分词作形容词）

senses.title: To hold attention completely
senses.definition: to interest someone so strongly that they cannot look away
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地吸引某人，使其无法移开目光
senses.example: The snake fascinated the bird.
senses.why: The spell holds the eyes; fascination is attention that cannot escape.
senses.whyCN: 咒语锁住目光；着迷是无法逃脱的注意。

senses.title: To charm or enchant
senses.definition: to fill with delight and wonder
senses.definitionCN: 以愉悦与惊奇充满内心
senses.example: She was fascinated by the northern lights.
senses.why: The old magic survives as wonder: enchantment without the witch.
senses.whyCN: 古老的魔法以惊奇存留：没有巫师的迷醉。

senses.title: To capture as if by a spell
senses.definition: to render unable to move or think clearly, as if under a spell
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛中了咒般无法动弹或清晰思考
senses.example: The crowd stood fascinated, unable to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 人群着了迷般站着，无法离开。
senses.why: The literal spell sense shows itself when willpower disappears.
senses.whyCN: 当意志力消失时，字面意义的咒术义便现身。

intro.en: Fascinate goes back to Latin fascinare, 'to cast a spell on', from fascinum, the evil spell or the charm against it.
intro.cn: fascinate 回溯拉丁语 fascinare「施咒」，出自 fascinum，即邪咒（或避邪的护符）。

items.en: Latin fascinum meant a spell or witchcraft; fascinare meant to enchant.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fascinum 指咒术；fascinare 意为施魔法迷住。

items.en: Late Latin fascinatus named one who has been enchanted.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 fascinatus 指被施了魔法之人。

items.en: Old French fasciner kept the sense of bewitching.
items.cn: 古法语 fasciner 保留「迷惑」之义。

items.en: Middle English fascinate meant to bewitch or cast a spell on someone.
items.cn: 中古英语 fascinate 意为对某人施咒。

items.en: Modern English weakened the magic into pure attraction: fascinated by a story, an idea, a face.
items.cn: 现代英语把魔法弱化为纯粹的吸引：被故事、想法或面孔迷住。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fasc- root (spell, bewitch); near-meaning words name degrees of captured attention.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fasc- 词根（施咒、迷住）；近义组命名注意力被俘获的不同程度。

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for casting spells.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「施咒」之词，五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin fascinare meant to cast a spell; fascinate still casts one on your eyes.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fascinare＝施咒；fascinate 至今仍在你的眼睛上施咒。

normal.en: be fascinated by is the everyday pattern: fascinated by stars, by history.
normal.cn: be fascinated by 是日常句型：被星星、历史迷住。

normal.en: captivate and fascinate are twins: both seize your attention.
normal.cn: captivate 与 fascinate 是双胞胎：都俘获注意力。

normal.en: a fascinating book keeps you up too late.
normal.cn: a fascinating book 让你熬夜。

normal.en: fascination is the noun: a lifelong fascination with trains.
normal.cn: fascination 是名词：对火车一生一世的痴迷。

abstract.en: A spell is attention that has forgotten how to leave.
abstract.cn: 咒语是忘了如何离开的注意力。

abstract.en: Fascination is gravity for the eyes.
abstract.cn: 着迷是眼睛的引力。

abstract.en: Wonder is magic that gave up its wand and stayed.
abstract.cn: 惊奇是交出魔杖却不肯离场的魔法。

examples.en: The old map fascinated everyone in the museum.
examples.cn: 那张古地图让博物馆里的每个人都着了迷。

examples.en: He was fascinated by the way ants build their cities.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁筑巢的方式让他着迷。

examples.en: Her fascinating lecture made the hours disappear.
examples.cn: 她引人入胜的讲座让几个小时悄然流逝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法斯内特」——法术迅速内摄心神（fast in-net），一下把你网住 → 使着迷。

root: 拉丁语 fascinare（施咒迷住），出自 fascinum（咒术；护符）。经后期拉丁语与古法语 fasciner 进入英语，本义为施魔法，现代英语弱化为纯粹的强烈吸引。

sensesIntro.en: From casting spells outward to charm, wonder, and attention that cannot escape.
sensesIntro.cn: 从施咒扩展到迷醉、惊奇与无法逃脱的注意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes caught by firelight, too deep in to look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光被火光俘获，深陷其中无法移开。

branches.en: THE GAZE HELD: attention that cannot leave.
branches.cn: 被锁的目光：无法离开的注意。

branches.en: THE DELIGHT: enchantment softened into joy.
branches.cn: 迷醉：魔法软化为喜悦。

branches.en: THE SPELL: the literal magic of immobility.
branches.cn: 咒语：无法动弹的字面魔法。

branches.en: THE CHARM: attraction and wonder in one word.
branches.cn: 魅力：吸引与惊奇集于一词。

branches.en: THE CAPTURE: the mind taken whole.
branches.cn: 俘获：整颗心被拿住。

intro.en: Fascinate is the fasc- spell root in a verb suit; the family keeps its magical flavor.

senses.title: Moving or able to move quickly
senses.definition: moving or able to move at high speed
senses.definitionCN: 以高速运动或能够高速运动
senses.example: A fast train saved us an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一趟快车为我们省了一小时。
senses.why: Strong motion is vigorous motion; vigor became velocity.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的动作即有力之动作；力转化为速。

senses.title: Happening or completed quickly
senses.definition: happening in a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内发生
senses.example: The dye is fast — no wait, the cure was fast.
senses.why: Time measured against events: quick deeds take little of it.
senses.whyCN: 以事件度量时间：迅速之事耗时少。

senses.title: Firmly fixed; not coming loose
senses.definition: firmly fixed or fastened; also of colour, not fading
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢固定的；（颜色）不褪的
senses.example: The roots held fast in the rock.
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the one speed grew out of and never replaced.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，速度义从它长出，却从未取代它。

senses.title: (Of a clock) ahead of the correct time
senses.definition: showing a time later than the true one
senses.definitionCN: 所显示时间比真实时间晚
senses.example: My watch is five minutes fast.
senses.why: A clock that runs with extra vigor runs ahead.
senses.whyCN: 跑得太有劲的钟，就跑到了时间前面。

senses.title: To abstain from food (noun/verb)
senses.definition: to eat no food for a period, as a religious duty or protest
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间不进食，或出于宗教义务或抗议
senses.example: They fast during the holy month.
senses.why: A separate homograph: the same letters, another word from Germanic fästan, 'to hold firm' (in self-control).
senses.whyCN: 另一同形词：同样字母，出自日耳曼语 fästan「坚定持守」（于自律之中）。

intro.en: Fast is a native English word whose oldest sense was 'firm, fixed'; speed came later by a strange road through advverbs of 'strongly'.
intro.cn: fast 是英语本族词，最古老的义项是「牢固的」；「迅速」经由「强有力地」这条奇特道路后来才长出。

items.en: The reconstructed root fastu- meant firm, steadfast.
items.cn: 重构词根 fastu- 意为牢固的、坚定的。

items.en: Old English fæst meant firm and secure: fast in the ground, hold fast.
items.cn: 古英语 fæst 意为牢固：牢牢扎根、抓紧（hold fast）。

items.en: Middle English adverb faste meant strongly, vigorously — and so, with quick action, swiftly.
items.cn: 中古英语副词 faste 意为用力地、 vigorous——动作迅捷时便有了「快」。

items.en: By Shakespeare's time fast for speed was common, though 'firm' senses lived on: stuck fast, hold fast.
items.cn: 到莎士比亚时代，fast 表「快」已很普遍，但「牢固」义仍在：stuck fast、hold fast。

items.en: Modern English fast leads with speed, while steadfast, fasten, and fast asleep guard the old firm sense.
items.cn: 现代英语以「快」为主导，而 steadfast、fasten、fast asleep 守护着古老的「牢固」义。

note.en: Look-alikes share the single syllable; near-meaning words name speed and the holding-fast that history left behind.
note.cn: 形近组共享单音节外形；近义组命名速度与历史留下的「牢固」义。

normalIntro.en: Five grips on one syllable that means both quick and firm.
normalIntro.cn: 又快又牢的单音节词，五个抓手。

normal.en: fast once meant firm: hold fast comes before run fast.
normal.cn: fast 先有「牢」义：hold fast 早于 run fast。

normal.en: fast asleep means deeply asleep, from the old firm sense.
normal.cn: fast asleep 意为「睡得很沉」，用的是旧「牢」义。

normal.en: breakfast is break plus fast: you break the night's fasting.
normal.cn: breakfast＝break+fast：结束整夜的斋戒。

normal.en: a fast colour never fades; a fast knot never slips.
normal.cn: fast colour 不褪色，fast knot 不松脱。

normal.en: My watch is fast means it runs ahead of time.
normal.cn: my watch is fast 指表走快了。

abstract.en: Speed and firmness meet in one word: things held tight move tight.
abstract.cn: 快与牢在一个词中相遇：抓得紧的东西动得利落。

abstract.en: A fast runner and a fast knot both refuse to let go — of time, of rope.
abstract.cn: 快人与快结都不肯松手——一个不肯松开时间，一个不肯松开绳子。

abstract.en: Fasting is holding firm against hunger.
abstract.cn: 斋戒是对饥饿坚定地持守。

examples.en: The fast current carried the leaf away in seconds.
examples.cn: 湍急的水流几秒内就把树叶带走。

examples.en: She held fast to the rope during the climb.
examples.cn: 攀爬时她紧紧抓住绳子。

examples.en: Members of the group fast on the first day of each month.
examples.cn: 该团体成员每月第一天斋戒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法斯特」——法（牢）+ 斯特（快）：既牢又快，fast 一词两义。

root: 原始日耳曼语 fastu-（牢固的）进入古英语 fæst。本义「牢固」，副词「用力地」在动作语境中演变为「迅速」。「斋戒」义为另一同形词，出自日耳曼语 fästan「坚定持守」。

sensesIntro.en: From firm holding outward through vigor to speed, ahead-of-time clocks, and self-denial.
sensesIntro.cn: 从牢固持守经「有力」抵达速度、走快的钟表与自我节制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grip so strong it becomes speed, and a will so firm it refuses food.
core.cn: 核心意象：抓得太牢便成了速度，意志太坚定便拒绝食物。

branches.en: THE SPEED: the everyday winner.
branches.cn: 速度：日常的主导义。

branches.en: THE QUICK EVENT: done in little time.
branches.cn: 迅速之事：耗时短。

branches.en: THE FIRM: the oldest root sense.
branches.cn: 牢固：最古老的词根义。

branches.en: THE AHEAD CLOCK: running before time.
branches.cn: 走快的钟：跑在时间之前。

branches.en: THE HOMOGRAPH: fasting, the other word in the same clothes.
branches.cn: 同形词：斋戒，同一件外衣里的另一个词。

intro.en: Fast is a bare Germanic root; its compounds fasten, steadfast, and breakfast all guard the old 'firm' sense.
intro.cn: fast 是裸的日耳曼词根；复合词 fasten、steadfast、breakfast 都守着旧的「牢固」义。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no member of this Germanic family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这个日耳曼词族中没有成员。

definition_en: having much flesh, the oily substance itself, or thick and rich in amount
core_image: 冬天里囤满脂肪的圆滚滚的刺猬，蜷成一团毛茸茸的球
scene: 生物课上显微镜下看到脂肪细胞，同学们围着图谱讨论能量储备。The slide showed fat cells storing energy for the body.
sceneCN: 这里指「脂肪」，对应第 2 个义项：体内储存能量的油脂组织；句意为切片显示脂肪细胞为身体储存能量。画面要点：显微镜、圆形细胞、生物图谱。

senses.title: Having much flesh on the body
senses.definition: having too much flesh on the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体上有过多肉
senses.example: The fat cat slept all afternoon.
senses.why: The stuffed root says it: overfilled with flesh.
senses.whyCN: 塞满的词根道出一词：肉被填得过多。

senses.title: Oily substance in animals and food
senses.definition: the oily part of animal bodies or food
senses.definitionCN: 动物体内或食物中的油脂部分
senses.example: Trim the fat off the meat.
senses.why: The noun keeps the substance behind the shape.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了形状背后的物质。

senses.title: Thick or wide
senses.definition: thick, broad, or swollen in shape
senses.definitionCN: 粗、宽或肿胀的形状
senses.example: A fat dictionary sat on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 书架上立着一本厚词典。
senses.why: Fullness of flesh becomes fullness of volume.
senses.whyCN: 肉身的丰满变成体积的丰满。

senses.title: Rich, abundant, or profitable
senses.definition: large in amount or very productive
senses.definitionCN: 数量大或非常肥沃多产
senses.example: The firm earned a fat profit.
senses.why: Well-fed land and well-fed accounts grow from the same stuffing.
senses.whyCN: 养肥的土地与养肥的账户出自同一次填塞。

intro.en: Fat is a native Germanic word, from a root meaning to stuff or cram, recorded in Old English as fæt.
intro.cn: fat 是日耳曼本族词，词根意为塞满、填实，古英语记作 fæt。

items.en: The reconstructed root fed- meant to stuff, to fatten.
items.cn: 重构词根 fed- 意为塞满、养肥。

items.en: Old English fæt meant well-fed, plump, and also the oily substance itself.
items.cn: 古英语 fæt 意为肥硕的，也指油脂本身。

items.en: Norse feitr reinforced the adjective in the north.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 feitr 在北方加固了该形容词。

items.en: Middle English fat covered the animal fat, the plump body, and rich land.
items.cn: 中古英语 fat 兼指动物脂肪、丰满身体与沃土。

items.en: Modern English extended fat to rich profits and thick letters: a fat salary, fat type.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fat 扩展到丰厚利润与粗壮字体：a fat salary、fat type。

note.en: Look-alikes share the single vowel; near-meaning words name plumpness of bodies and richness of soils and profits.
note.cn: 形近组共享单元音外形；近义组命名身体的丰满与土壤、利润的肥沃丰厚。

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Germanic word for being stuffed full.
normalIntro.cn: 日耳曼语「被塞满」之词，五个抓手。

normal.en: fat comes from a root meaning to stuff: a fat body is an overfilled one.
normal.cn: fat 的词根意为塞满：胖就是被填得过多。

normal.en: fat has a noun side: the fat on meat, fats in food.
normal.cn: fat 有名词面：肉上的肥肉、食物中的油脂。

normal.en: a fat salary and fat profits mean rich and plenty.
normal.cn: a fat salary、fat profits 表示丰厚、大量。

normal.en: fat chance is irony: it means no chance at all.
normal.cn: fat chance 是反讽：意思是毫无机会。

normal.en: chew the fat means to chat idly.
normal.cn: chew the fat 意为闲聊。

abstract.en: Fat is the body's bank account, deposits of summer spent in winter.
abstract.cn: 脂肪是身体的银行账户：夏天存入，冬天支取。

abstract.en: Richness always looks stuffed: full land, full purse, full shape.
abstract.cn: 丰饶总是显得被塞满：满的土地、满的钱袋、满的形体。

abstract.en: Fatten and fatten: the farmer fattens the pig, the year fattens the account.
abstract.cn: 同一个 fatten：农民把猪养肥，岁月把账户养肥。

examples.en: Too much fat in the diet is bad for the heart.
examples.cn: 饮食中脂肪过多对心脏不好。

examples.en: The fat envelope held all four letters of acceptance.
examples.cn: 厚厚的信封装着四封录取信。

examples.en: The company reported a fat surplus at year end.
examples.cn: 公司年终报告了丰厚的盈余。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法特」——法式大餐吃特多，人就 fat（胖）。

root: 原始日耳曼语 fed-（塞满、养肥）进入古英语 fæt，经古诺斯语 feitr 加固。本义「被填满的」，由身体扩展到油脂、厚度、丰饶与利润。

sensesIntro.en: From stuffed bodies outward to oils, thickness, richness, and profit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从塞满的身体扩展到油脂、厚度、丰饶与利润。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing filled past its natural size.
core.cn: 核心意象：被填得超出本来尺寸之物。

branches.en: THE BODY: flesh in excess.
branches.cn: 身体：过多的肉。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: the oil itself.
branches.cn: 物质：油脂本身。

branches.en: THE VOLUME: thick and broad.
branches.cn: 体积：厚而宽。

branches.en: THE RICHNESS: fertile land, fat profit.
branches.cn: 丰饶：沃土与厚利。

branches.en: THE STUFFING: one act of filling behind all senses.
branches.cn: 填塞：所有义项背后同一次「填充」。

intro.en: Fat is a bare Germanic root; its family grows with simple suffixes.
intro.cn: fat 是裸的日耳曼词根；词族用简单后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no member of this Germanic family; adipose is the learned Latin word for fat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在此日耳曼词族中没有成员；书面语用 adipose 表示脂肪。

definition_zh: 父亲；爸爸；祖先；奠基者；神父
definition_en: a male parent, a male ancestor, a founder, or a priest
core_image: 宽厚的手掌搭在孩子肩上，黄昏的影子把两个人的身影连成一片
scene: 家长会上，父亲坐在小椅子上认真记笔记，孩子在窗外偷偷挥手。The father listened carefully to the teacher's advice.
sceneCN: 这里指「父亲」，对应第 1 个义项：男性亲长；句意为父亲认真听取老师的建议。画面要点：小椅子、笔记本、窗外挥手的身影。

senses.title: A male parent
senses.definition: a man who has a child; the male parent
senses.definitionCN: 有孩子之人；男性亲长
senses.example: His father taught him to swim.
senses.why: The core kinship sense, unchanged for thousands of years.
senses.whyCN: 核心亲属义，数千年未变。

senses.title: A male ancestor
senses.definition: a male forefather
senses.definitionCN: 男性祖先
senses.example: Our fathers settled this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的先辈开拓了这条山谷。
senses.why: One generation back becomes many: the parent of long ago.
senses.whyCN: 一代之上再推数代：久远年代的亲长。

senses.title: A founder or originator
senses.definition: the man who began or created something important
senses.definitionCN: 开创或创造某重要事物之人
senses.example: Freud is called the father of psychoanalysis.
senses.exampleCN: 弗洛伊德被称为精神分析之父。
senses.why: Parenthood applied to ideas: to father a school of thought.
senses.whyCN: 亲长之义用于思想：孕育一个学派。

senses.title: A priest or elder of the church
senses.definition: a priest, or a title of respect for clergy
senses.definitionCN: 神父，或对教士的尊称
senses.example: Father Brown is a famous fictional priest.
senses.exampleCN: 布朗神父是著名的虚构神父。
senses.why: The church made fathers of its shepherds.
senses.whyCN: 教会把牧者尊为父。

senses.title: To act as a father to; to be the father of
senses.definition: to care for someone as a father, or to father a child
senses.definitionCN: 像父亲般照料某人，或成为孩子的父亲
senses.example: He fathered the orphaned team like family.
senses.exampleCN: 他像家人一样照顾失去教练的队伍。
senses.why: The noun steps into the verb position and performs the care itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词登上动词之位，亲自履行照料。

items.en: Middle English fader covered parent, ancestor, and revered elders.

normal.cn: father、拉丁 pater、希腊 patēr 出自同一个史前词根。

normal.en: father can mean founder: the father of modern science.

normal.en: like father, like son pairs the oldest kinship with an old proverb.

abstract.en: A father is a first mountain: you climb away from it, and it keeps shaping your horizon.
abstract.cn: 父亲是第一座山：你离开它去攀登，它却一直在塑造你的地平线。

abstract.en: Ideas have fathers too; every theory begins as someone's child.
abstract.cn: 思想也有父亲；每个理论最初都是某个人的孩子。

abstract.en: To father is to stand where care and origin meet.
abstract.cn: 成为父亲，就是站在照料与起源的交汇处。

examples.en: My father taught me to ride a bike in the park.
examples.cn: 我父亲在公园里教我骑自行车。

examples.en: The fathers of the town built the first school here.
examples.cn: 小镇的先辈们在这里建起了第一所学校。

examples.en: Confucius is regarded as the father of Chinese education.
examples.cn: 孔子被视为中国教育之父。
